### 🤖 Assistant
*2026-10-07 16:11:56*

Actúa como Senior Frontend Engineer especializado en Next.js App Router, TypeScript y Tailwind CSS.

Necesito implementar la **Fase 2: Shell del Negocio y UI Base (Multi-Tenant)** para la plataforma SaaS **NEXUS THRIVE**.

## Contexto del proyecto

* **Framework:** Next.js con App Router
* **Lenguaje:** TypeScript
* **Estilos:** Tailwind CSS
* **Iconos:** `lucide-react`
* **Autenticación:** `@clerk/nextjs`
* **Arquitectura:** Multi-tenant
* **Rutas:** `app/[tenant]/...`
* `[tenant]` representa el slug del negocio, obtenido a partir del subdominio.
* Ejemplo:

  * `gymcarlos.lvh.me:3000`
  * `gymcarlos.nexusthrive.com.co`

## Diseño y experiencia visual

Construye una interfaz de dashboard SaaS:

* Moderna
* Limpia
* Profesional
* Minimalista
* Responsive
* Modo claro
* Buena jerarquía visual
* Excelente experiencia en desktop y mobile

Paleta principal:

* Slate para textos, bordes y superficies
* Indigo como color principal de interacción
* Emerald para estados positivos y elementos activos
* White para superficies principales

Utiliza `lucide-react` para iconos en lugar de SVGs manuales cuando exista un icono equivalente.

---

# Componentes a crear

## 1. Header

Archivo:

```text
app/components/tenant/header.tsx
```

Características:

* Debe ser un **Client Component**.
* Debe comenzar con:

```tsx
"use client";
```

* Debe mostrar:

  * Logo/nombre de NEXUS THRIVE
  * Nombre del negocio activo
  * Badge de estado `"Activo"`
  * `UserButton` de Clerk
  * Botón de menú para mobile
* Debe ser responsive.
* El menú mobile debe poder abrirse y cerrarse mediante estado local con `useState`.
* Utiliza iconos de `lucide-react`.
* No debe importar:

  * `@clerk/nextjs/server`
  * Prisma
  * `db`
  * lógica de acceso a base de datos
  * módulos server-only

El componente debe recibir únicamente datos serializables necesarios para la UI.

Por ejemplo:

```tsx
type HeaderProps = {
  tenantName: string;
};
```

No pases directamente objetos completos provenientes de Prisma al Client Component, especialmente si contienen `Temporal.Instant`, `Date` u otros objetos no serializables.

---

## 2. Sidebar

Crear:

```text
app/components/tenant/sidebar.tsx
```

Debe funcionar como navegación principal del negocio.

Secciones:

* Dashboard
* CRM
* Finanzas
* Inventario
* Configuración

Cada sección debe incluir su icono correspondiente de `lucide-react`.

Ejemplo:

```text
Dashboard
CRM
Finanzas
Inventario
Configuración
```

Características:

* Desktop:

  * Sidebar fija o sticky
  * Ancho aproximado de `240px` a `280px`
* Mobile:

  * Oculta inicialmente
  * Puede abrirse desde el Header
  * Debe incluir overlay cuando esté abierta
* La navegación debe utilizar rutas relativas al tenant:

```text
/[tenant]
/[tenant]/crm
/[tenant]/finance
/[tenant]/inventory
/[tenant]/settings
```

No hardcodees `gymcarlos`.

El componente debe recibir el slug del tenant o utilizar una estrategia compatible con la arquitectura existente.

---

# 3. Layout del Tenant

Modificar:

```text
app/[tenant]/layout.tsx
```

Este archivo debe permanecer como **Server Component**.

NO agregar:

```tsx
"use client";
```

Debe encargarse de:

1. Obtener el tenant desde el slug.
2. Validar que el tenant exista.
3. Validar que esté activo.
4. Obtener el usuario autenticado mediante Clerk.
5. Resolver el usuario local asociado al tenant.
6. Crear/usar el contexto de acceso del tenant.
7. Renderizar el Header.
8. Renderizar el Sidebar.
9. Renderizar `{children}` dentro del área principal.

Mantén toda la lógica server-side aquí.

No muevas Prisma, `auth()`, `currentUser()` ni `createTenantDb()` a componentes cliente.

---

# 4. Dashboard principal

Modificar:

```text
app/[tenant]/page.tsx
```

Crear un dashboard inicial profesional.

Debe contener:

## Header del dashboard

* Saludo al usuario
* Nombre del negocio
* Descripción breve

Ejemplo conceptual:

```text
Buenos días, Carlos

Aquí tienes un resumen de tu negocio.
```

## Cards de métricas

Crear inicialmente:

* Ingresos
* Clientes
* Gastos
* Balance

Cada card debe tener:

* Icono
* Título
* Valor
* Indicador visual
* Pequeña descripción secundaria

Los valores pueden ser placeholders inicialmente si todavía no existen los repositorios necesarios.

No inventes datos reales de negocio.

---

# 5. Actividad reciente

Crear una sección:

```text
Actividad reciente
```

Puede utilizar datos mock temporales si todavía no existe la capa de datos correspondiente.

Ejemplos conceptuales:

* Nuevo cliente registrado
* Pago recibido
* Gasto registrado
* Factura creada

Los mocks deben estar claramente aislados para poder reemplazarlos posteriormente por datos reales.

---

# 6. Acciones rápidas

Crear una sección:

```text
Acciones rápidas
```

Con acciones como:

* Nuevo cliente
* Registrar pago
* Registrar gasto
* Crear factura

Utilizar botones visualmente consistentes con el diseño general.

---

# Arquitectura y restricciones

Respeta estrictamente la separación entre Server Components y Client Components.

## Server Components

Pueden utilizar:

```tsx
@clerk/nextjs/server
```

Prisma:

```tsx
@/prisma/db
```

y:

```tsx
@/lib/tenant-db
```

## Client Components

NO pueden importar:

```tsx
@clerk/nextjs/server
```

ni:

```tsx
@/prisma/db
```

ni ningún módulo `server-only`.

Los datos enviados desde Server Components a Client Components deben ser serializables.

Por ejemplo:

```tsx
<Header tenantName={tenantRecord.name} />
```

NO:

```tsx
<Header tenantRecord={tenantRecord} />
```

si `tenantRecord` contiene valores como:

```text
Temporal.Instant
Date
Decimal
```

---

# Responsive Design

La interfaz debe funcionar correctamente en:

* Desktop
* Laptop
* Tablet
* Mobile

Breakpoints de Tailwind:

```text
sm
md
lg
xl
```

En mobile:

* Sidebar cerrada inicialmente
* Header simplificado
* Contenido con padding reducido
* Cards adaptadas a una columna

En desktop:

* Sidebar visible
* Header completo
* Dashboard utilizando grid
* Aprovechar correctamente el espacio disponible

---

# Calidad del código

Utiliza:

* TypeScript estricto
* Componentes reutilizables
* Props tipadas
* `lucide-react`
* Tailwind CSS
* Nombres descriptivos
* Código limpio
* Sin duplicación innecesaria

No introduzcas librerías nuevas si no son necesarias.

No cambies:

* Prisma
* esquema de base de datos
* middleware/proxy
* configuración de Clerk
* arquitectura multi-tenant

salvo que sea estrictamente necesario para completar esta fase.

---

# Resultado esperado

La estructura final debería aproximarse a:

```text
app/
├── components/
│   └── tenant/
│       ├── header.tsx
│       └── sidebar.tsx
│
└── [tenant]/
    ├── layout.tsx
    ├── page.tsx
    ├── crm/
    ├── finance/
    ├── inventory/
    └── settings/
```

El resultado debe sentirse como el **panel real de una plataforma SaaS profesional**, no como una plantilla genérica de Next.js.

Prioriza:

1. Arquitectura correcta Server/Client.
2. Multi-tenancy seguro.
3. UX profesional.
4. Responsive design.
5. Componentización.
6. Código mantenible.

Antes de modificar archivos, inspecciona la estructura existente y reutiliza los componentes y patrones que ya existen. No sobrescribas lógica existente innecesariamente.

Si encuentras un conflicto entre los requerimientos de UI y la arquitectura existente, prioriza la arquitectura multi-tenant y la separación Server/Client.

7: 
8: ```tsx filename="app/example-client-component.tsx" switcher
9: 'use client'
10: 
11: import { usePathname } from 'next/navigation'
12: 
13: export default function ExampleClientComponent() {
14:   const pathname = usePathname()
15:   return <p>Current pathname: {pathname}</p>
16: }
17: ```
18: 
19: ```jsx filename="app/example-client-component.js" switcher
20: 'use client'
21: 
22: import { usePathname } from 'next/navigation'
23: 
24: export default function ExampleClientComponent() {
25:   const pathname = usePathname()
26:   return <p>Current pathname: {pathname}</p>
27: }
28: ```
29: 
30: `usePathname` intentionally requires using a [Client Component](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components). It's important to note Client Components are not a de-optimization. They are an integral part of the [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) architecture.
31: 
32: For example, a Client Component with `usePathname` will be rendered into HTML on the initial page load. When navigating to a new route, this component does not need to be re-fetched. Instead, the component is downloaded once (in the client JavaScript bundle), and re-renders based on the current state.
33: 
34: > **Good to know**:
35: >
36: > - Reading the current URL from a [Server Component](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) is not supported. This design is intentional to support layout state being preserved across page navigations.
37: > - If your page is being statically prerendered and your app has [rewrites](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/rewrites) in `next.config` or a [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy) file, reading the pathname with `usePathname()` can result in hydration mismatch errors, because the initial value comes from the server and may not match the actual browser pathname after routing. See our [example](#avoid-hydration-mismatch-with-rewrites) for a way to mitigate this issue.
38: 
39: <details>
40: 
41: <summary>Compatibility with Pages Router</summary>
42: 
43: If you have components that use `usePathname` and they are imported into routes within the Pages Router, be aware that `usePathname` may return `null` if the router is not yet initialized. This can occur in cases such as [fallback routes](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths#fallback-true) or during [Automatic Static Optimization](/docs/pages/building-your-application/rendering/automatic-static-optimization) in the Pages Router.
44: 
45: To enhance compatibility between routing systems, if your project contains both an `app` and a `pages` directory, Next.js will automatically adjust the return type of `usePathname`.
46: 
47: </details>
48: 
49: ## Parameters
50: 
51: ```tsx
52: const pathname = usePathname()
53: ```
54: 
55: `usePathname` does not take any parameters.
56: 
57: ## Returns
58: 
59: `usePathname` returns a string of the current URL's pathname. For example:
60: 
61: | URL                 | Returned value        |
62: | ------------------- | --------------------- |
63: | `/`                 | `'/'`                 |
64: | `/dashboard`        | `'/dashboard'`        |
65: | `/dashboard?v=2`    | `'/dashboard'`        |
66: | `/blog/hello-world` | `'/blog/hello-world'` |
67: 
68: ## Behavior
69: 
70: ### Cache Components
71: 
72: When [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, `usePathname` may require a [`Suspense`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary. This depends on whether the pathname can be resolved during prerendering.
73: 
74: - **Static routes and routes with [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params)**: every route segment, including dynamic params, is known at build time. The pathname can be resolved during prerendering, so `usePathname` resolves on the server and no `Suspense` boundary is required.
75: - **Routes with dynamic params not covered by `generateStaticParams`**: the param is a [fallback param](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params#all-paths-at-build-time) that is not known until request time. The pathname cannot be resolved during prerendering, so `usePathname` suspends. Wrap the component (or a parent) in a `Suspense` boundary so its fallback can be rendered during prerendering; otherwise, the build fails.
76: 
77: This applies even when the component that calls `usePathname` is itself static. For example, a sidebar with active links rendered in a layout suspends on any page below it that has an unknown dynamic param. To keep the rest of the layout prerendered, wrap the component that calls `usePathname` (or a parent) in a `Suspense` boundary with a fallback.
78: 
79: See [Next.js encountered URL data in a Client Component outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-client-hook) for full fix options and trade-offs.
80: 
81: ## Examples
82: 
83: ### Do something in response to a route change
84: 
85: ```tsx filename="app/example-client-component.tsx" switcher
86: 'use client'
87: 
88: import { useEffect } from 'react'
89: import { usePathname, useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation'
90: 
91: function ExampleClientComponent() {
92:   const pathname = usePathname()
93:   const searchParams = useSearchParams()
94:   useEffect(() => {
95:     // Do something here...
96:   }, [pathname, searchParams])
97: }
98: ```
99: 
100: ```jsx filename="app/example-client-component.js" switcher
101: 'use client'
102: 
103: import { useEffect } from 'react'
104: import { usePathname, useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation'
105: 
106: function ExampleClientComponent() {
107:   const pathname = usePathname()
108:   const searchParams = useSearchParams()
109:   useEffect(() => {
110:     // Do something here...
111:   }, [pathname, searchParams])
112: }
113: ```
114: 
115: ### Avoid hydration mismatch with rewrites
116: 
117: When a page is prerendered, the HTML is generated for the source pathname. If the page is then reached through a rewrite using `next.config` or `Proxy`, the browser URL may differ, and `usePathname()` will read the rewritten pathname on the client.
118: 
119: To avoid hydration mismatches, design the UI so that only a small, isolated part depends on the client pathname. Render a stable fallback on the server and update that part after mount. The deferred read shows a brief moment of the fallback before the real pathname appears; see [Preventing flash before hydration](/docs/app/guides/preventing-flash-before-hydration) for techniques that eliminate the visible flicker.
120: 
121: ```tsx filename="app/example-client-component.tsx" switcher
122: 'use client'
123: 
124: import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
125: import { usePathname } from 'next/navigation'
126: 
127: export default function PathnameBadge() {
128:   const pathname = usePathname()
129:   const [clientPathname, setClientPathname] = useState('')
130: 
131:   useEffect(() => {
132:     setClientPathname(pathname)
133:   }, [pathname])
134: 
135:   return (
136:     <p>
137:       Current pathname: <span>{clientPathname}</span>
138:     </p>
139:   )
140: }
141: ```
142: 
143: ```jsx filename="app/example-client-component.js" switcher
144: 'use client'
145: 
146: import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
147: import { usePathname } from 'next/navigation'
148: 
149: export default function PathnameBadge() {
150:   const pathname = usePathname()
151:   const [clientPathname, setClientPathname] = useState('')
152: 
153:   useEffect(() => {
154:     setClientPathname(pathname)
155:   }, [pathname])
156: 
157:   return (
158:     <p>
159:       Current pathname: <span>{clientPathname}</span>
160:     </p>
161:   )
162: }
163: ```
164: 
165: | Version   | Changes                   |
166: | --------- | ------------------------- |
167: | `v13.0.0` | `usePathname` introduced. |

### `app/components/tenant/sidebar-context.tsx`

```tsx
"use client";

import { createContext, useCallback, useContext, useMemo, useState } from "react";

type SidebarContextValue = {
  isOpen: boolean;
  open: () => void;
  close: () => void;
  toggle: () => void;
};

const SidebarContext = createContext<SidebarContextValue | null>(null);

export function SidebarProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
  const open = useCallback(() => setIsOpen(true), []);
  const close = useCallback(() => setIsOpen(false), []);
  const toggle = useCallback(() => setIsOpen(v => !v), []);
  const value = useMemo(() => ({isOpen, open, close, toggle}), [isOpen, open, close, toggle]);
  return <SidebarContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</SidebarContext.Provider>;
}

export function useSidebar(): SidebarContextValue {
  const ctx = useContext(SidebarContext);
  if (!ctx) throw new Error("useSidebar debe usarse dentro de <SidebarProvider>");
  return ctx;
}
```

### Body scroll lock on mobile drawer open:
```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (!isOpen) return;
  const previous = document.body.style.overflow;
  document.body.style.overflow = "hidden";
  const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => { if (e.key === "Escape") close(); };
  window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
  return () => { document.body.style.overflow = previous; window.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey); };
}, [isOpen, close]);
```
Note: on desktop, isOpen stays false normally (toggle button hidden) ✓. But if user opens drawer at mobile then resizes to desktop → body overflow hidden + drawer visible (translate-x-0 due to lg:translate-x-0) → body scroll locked on desktop! Fix: also close on pathname change; and could handle resize... Simple: lock only when isOpen; if resized to lg, `lg:translate-x-0` shows it anyway and body locked → bad edge case.

Mitigation: lock scroll only below lg? Use `window.matchMedia("(min-width: 1024px)")` → if matches, don't lock; and close drawer on resize to desktop:
```ts
const mq = window.matchMedia("(min-width: 1024px)");
const onChange = () => { if (mq.matches) close(); };
mq.addEventListener("change", onChange);
```
Nice touch, small. I'll include resize-close (also unlocks scroll naturally since isOpen false).

Also close on pathname change:
```ts
const pathname = usePathname();
useEffect(() => { close(); }, [pathname, close]);
```

if (subdomain && subdomain !== "app" && subdomain !== "www") {

  return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL(`${tenantPrefix}${pathname}`, request.url));
}

<content>
1: # Prisma 8 — Queries (Postgres)
2: 
3: > Load this guide when `db.ts` imports from `@internal/postgres/runtime`.
4: 
5: Shared concepts (result consumption, script teardown, cross-target pitfalls, capability gaps) live in [`queries.md`](./queries.md).
6: 
7: ## Key Concepts
8: 
9: **Postgres** (`postgres<Contract>(...)` from `@internal/postgres/runtime`):
10: 
11: - **`db.orm.<ns>.<Model>`** — ORM, PascalCase model name (`db.orm.public.User`). Fluent `.where(...).select(...).orderBy(...).all()`, fully typed against `Contract`. Default lane for CRUD with relations.
12: - **`db.sql.<ns>.<table>`** — SQL builder, lowercase storage name (`db.sql.public.user`). Produces a *plan*. A plan that returns rows (`select`, or a write with `.returning(...)`) runs through `db.runtime().query(plan)`; a write with no `RETURNING` runs through `db.runtime().execute(plan)`, which resolves `{ affectedRows }`. Use when the ORM is too high-level — explicit `JOIN`, computed projections, set operations, window functions.
13: 
14: Reach for the ORM first; drop to `db.sql` when the ORM can't express the shape. Lane choice is local — one query function picks one lane, not the whole app.
15: 
16: **Lane decision table:**
17: 
18: | Need | Choose | Why |
19: | --- | --- | --- |
20: | Standard CRUD with relations | **ORM (`db.orm.<ns>.<Model>`)** | Highest ergonomics; fully typed; model-shaped. |
21: | Eager-load related records | **ORM `.include(...)`** | Composes with `.where` / `.select` / `.orderBy` / `.limit` per branch. |
22: | Aggregate (count, sum, avg) | **ORM `.aggregate(...)`** | Typed result; works with grouping (`.groupBy(...).aggregate(...)`). |
23: | `INSERT ... RETURNING` / `UPDATE ... RETURNING` typed result | **ORM mutations** (returns updated rows) or **`db.sql.<ns>.<t>.insert(...).returning(...)`** | ORM returns inserted/updated rows; SQL builder exposes `.returning(...)` explicitly. |
24: | Computed projection (e.g. `ST_DistanceSphere(location, point) AS meters`) alongside model fields | **SQL builder (`db.sql.<ns>.<t>`)** | The ORM projects model fields; arbitrary expression projection is the SQL builder's seam. |
25: | Complex `JOIN`, set operation, window function | **SQL builder** | The ORM doesn't express arbitrary joins. |
26: | Postgres-specific feature (`LATERAL`, `FILTER`, custom aggregates) | **SQL builder**, falling back to extension operators when the extension provides them | DSL first; extensions can contribute operators (`postgis`, `pgvector`). |
27: 
28: ## Workflow — ORM reads
29: 
30: The concept: `db.orm.<ns>.<Model>` returns a *collection* you compose method-by-method. Each call returns a new collection (immutable chaining); the terminal verb (`.all()` / `.first()` / `.aggregate(...)`) issues the query. There is no `.count()` terminal on the collection — `count()` is an `include` reducer and an `aggregate(...)` operation (both below). Predicates are lambdas over a field proxy: `u.field.<op>(value)`.
31: 
32: ```typescript
33: // src/queries/users.ts — one directory deep under src/, so the import is '../prisma/db'
34: import { db } from '../prisma/db';
35: 
36: // Find one record by primary key shorthand.
37: const user = await db.orm.public.User.first({ id: userId });
38: // Returns the full row or `null`.
39: 
40: // Find one matching a predicate.
41: const alice = await db.orm.public.User
42:   .where((u) => u.email.eq('alice@example.com'))
43:   .first();
44: 
45: // Find many with projection, sort, and limit.
46: const recentUsers = await db.orm.public.User
47:   .select('id', 'email', 'createdAt')
48:   .orderBy((u) => u.createdAt.desc())
49:   .limit(10)
50:   .all();
51: ```
52: 
53: **Predicates** (`.where(...)`) come in two forms:
54: 
55: ```typescript
56: // Lambda form — full expression power.
57: db.orm.public.User.where((u) => u.email.eq('alice@example.com'));
58: 
59: // Shorthand object form — equality on the named fields.
60: db.orm.public.User.where({ kind: 'admin' });
61: ```
62: 
63: Operators on the field proxy include `.eq`, `.neq`, `.lt`, `.lte`, `.gt`, `.gte`, `.like`, `.ilike`, `.in([...])`, `.isNull()`, `.isNotNull()`. Extensions add target-specific operators on extension-typed columns (`pgvector`'s `.cosineDistance(...)`, `postgis`'s `.within(...)` / `.intersectsBbox(...)` / `.distanceSphere(...)`).
64: 
65: **Full-text search** is built into the Postgres target, on any text column: `.fullTextMatches(q)` is the predicate, `.fullTextRank(q)` scores a row so you can order by relevance, and `.fullTextHeadline(q)` returns the text with `<b>` around the matches. The argument `q` is a `tsquery`, built with a helper from `@prisma/orm-postgres/target/full-text`. A bare string is a type error, because Postgres would read it as `tsquery` syntax without lowercasing or stemming it. Pick the helper by where the text comes from:
66: 
67: - A search box: `websearchToTsquery(input)`. `"an exact phrase"`, `-excluded` and `or` work, and it never errors. `plaintoTsquery` requires every word; `phrasetoTsquery` requires the words in order.
68: - User input inside operator syntax, such as typeahead: the `tsquery` tag, `` tsquery`${term}:*` ``. The literal parts are trusted `tsquery` syntax you write. Each interpolated value becomes exactly one quoted term, so user input cannot add operators or break the syntax; an empty value adds no words, like a stop word. A value with several words becomes a phrase: `` tsquery`${'new y'}:*` `` gives `'new':* <-> 'y':*`, so the words must be adjacent and in order, and `:*` applies to each word. Do not put quotes around the interpolation yourself: `` tsquery`'${term}':*` `` is a syntax error for every input. Postgres `to_tsquery` then lowercases and stems every word. `` tsquery({ language: 'german' })`...` `` picks the configuration.
69: - Operator syntax you write in full: `toTsquery("'zebra' & !'graze'")`. Malformed text fails at execution, so never pass user input to it; use the `tsquery` tag for that.
70: 
71: The four parsers are also `fns` members in the SQL builder. Each takes the text (a string, or a text column of any kind, `varchar` included) and `{ language? }`, and binds the text as a parameter. The `tsquery` tag is an import in both the ORM and the SQL builder. A `tsquery` value read back from a query can be passed straight back as the query.
72: 
73: Each operation takes an options object as its second argument. `language` (default `'english'`) is the configuration for the column's `to_tsvector`, the expression the index covers; the parser's or tag's own `language` governs the query side, and the two normally match. It only accepts the configurations a stock PostgreSQL server ships with (`'simple'`, `'german'`, `'french'`, …); `fullTextRank` also takes `normalization` (the `ts_rank` bitmask, 0 to 63) and `coverDensity` (for `ts_rank_cd`); `fullTextHeadline` also takes `startSel`, `stopSel`, `maxWords`, `minWords` and `highlightAll`. Every one of them is written into the SQL as a literal, so anything invalid throws `RUNTIME.ARGUMENT_INVALID` when the query is built.
74: 
75: ```typescript
76: import { tsquery, websearchToTsquery } from '@prisma/orm-postgres/target/full-text';
77: 
78: // ORM: filter by the search-box query, order by relevance. Build the query once and reuse it.
79: const q = websearchToTsquery(query);
80: const hits = await db.orm.public.Message
81:   .select('id', 'text')
82:   .where((m) => m.text.fullTextMatches(q))
83:   .orderBy((m) => m.text.fullTextRank(q).desc())
84:   .limit(20)
85:   .all();
86: 
87: // ORM: typeahead, the typed text as a prefix term.
88: const suggestions = await db.orm.public.Message
89:   .select('id', 'text')
90:   .where((m) => m.text.fullTextMatches(tsquery`${term}:*`))
91:   .all();
92: 
93: // SQL builder: the same query filters and highlights, so the snippet marks what selected the row.
94: const snippets = db.sql.public.message
95:   .select('id')
96:   .select('snippet', (f, fns) =>
97:     fns.fullTextHeadline(f.text, q, { startSel: '<mark>', stopSel: '</mark>', maxWords: 20 }),
98:   )
99:   .where((f, fns) => fns.fullTextMatches(f.text, q))
100:   .build();
101: ```
102: 
103: Without an index Postgres recomputes `to_tsvector` for every row, and it only uses one whose expression is the same `to_tsvector` over the same configuration literal and the same column. `@@fullTextIndex` renders that expression for you — pass it the field and, if you use one, the same language:
104: 
105: ```prisma
106: @@fullTextIndex([text], name: "message_text_search")
107: @@fullTextIndex([text], where: "archived_at IS NULL", name: "message_text_search_live")
108: ```
109: 
110: Give the index and the operation the same `language`: a mismatch raises no error, the query silently falls back to a sequential scan.
111: 
112: In a TypeScript contract, the same helper from `@prisma/orm-postgres/contract-builder`:
113: 
114: ```typescript
115: model('Message', { fields: { id, text } }).sql(({ cols }) => ({
116:   indexes: [fullTextIndex(cols.text, { name: 'message_text_search' })],
117: }));
118: ```
119: 
120: **There is no `.between(a, b)` operator.** Express ranges either as two chained `.where(...)` clauses (the idiomatic form — clauses AND-compose) or with the `and(...)` combinator inside one clause:
121: 
122: ```typescript
123: // Chained .where() — each clause AND-composes with the previous one.
124: await db.orm.public.Sale
125:   .where((s) => s.day.gte(start))
126:   .where((s) => s.day.lte(end))
127:   .all();
128: 
129: // Equivalent with an explicit `and(...)` inside one clause.
130: import { and } from '@prisma/orm-postgres/orm-client';
131: await db.orm.public.Sale
132:   .where((s) => and(s.day.gte(start), s.day.lte(end)))
133:   .all();
134: ```
135: 
136: The two forms emit the same SQL. Pick chained `.where()` when each clause adds a separate condition that reads as its own thought; pick `and(...)` when one logical predicate happens to have two parts and you want the visual grouping. Don't reach for a `between` helper — there isn't one.
137: 
138: **Combinators** (`and`, `or`, `not`) compose predicates, and **relation predicates** (`.some(...)`, `.none(...)`, `.every(...)`) recurse into a relation. `.some()` and `.none()` take an optional predicate — `u.posts.none()` means "has no posts", `u.posts.some()` means "has at least one" — while `.every(...)` requires one: `u.posts.every((p) => p.published.eq(true))`. The combinators are exported from the façade's `orm-client` subpath:
139: 
140: ```typescript
141: import { and, or, not } from '@prisma/orm-postgres/orm-client';
142: 
143: await db.orm.public.User
144:   .where((u) =>
145:     and(
146:       or(u.kind.eq('admin'), u.email.ilike('%@example.com')),
147:       not(u.posts.none((p) => p.title.ilike('%draft%'))),
148:     ),
149:   )
150:   .all();
151: ```
152: 
153: **Sorting and pagination.** `.orderBy(...)` accepts a single lambda or an array of lambdas. Each calls `.asc()` / `.desc()` on a field, an extension-operation result, a to-one relation's field, or a to-many relation's `count(...)`. Every `.asc()` / `.desc()` takes `{ nulls: 'first' | 'last' }`. `.limit(n)` limits; `.offset(n)` offsets.
154:

179: **Ordering by a relation.** A to-one relation (`1:1`, `N:1`) exposes the related model's orderable fields; a to-many relation (`1:N`, `N:M`) exposes `count(predicate?)`, through the junction for `N:M`. One hop only. Each lowers to a correlated scalar subquery, so the main query gains no join.

199: A missing related row (null foreign key) orders as `NULL`. To-one relations have no `count`; to-many relations expose no fields.
200: 
201: Cursor keys must match fields in the active `orderBy`. For a composite `orderBy`, pass a value for each ordering column — a partial cursor seeks only on the columns you supply, which gives an incomplete keyset. An empty cursor object is a no-op: you get the unfiltered first page back. `cursor()` keys on plain columns only: it throws `ORM.ARGUMENT_INVALID` when an active order is a relation field, a relation `count(...)`, an extension-operation result (`fullTextRank`, vector distance) or sets `nulls`. `distinctOn()` throws the same only when one of its leading orders, as many as there are `distinctOn` columns, is not a plain column; relation, count and operation orders after them are fine. Paginate those orders with `.limit(n).offset(n)`.
202: 
203: **`.first()` vs `.first({ pk })` vs `.all()`.** Use `.first()` for a single row (issues a `LIMIT 1`); use `.first({ pk })` for primary-key lookups; reserve `.all()` for the genuine many case (no implicit `LIMIT`).
204: 
205: ## Workflow — Eager-loading relations (`.include`)
206: 
207: The concept: `.include('<relation>', (branch) => branch.<chain>)` adds a relation branch to the parent query. The branch is its own collection — compose `.where` / `.select` / `.orderBy` / `.limit` on it just like the parent.
208: 
209: ```typescript
210: await db.orm.public.User
211:   .select('id', 'email')
212:   .include('posts', (post) =>
213:     post
214:       .select('id', 'title', 'createdAt')
215:       .orderBy((p) => p.createdAt.desc())
216:       .limit(5),
217:   )
218:   .limit(10)
219:   .all();
220: // → Array<{ id, email, posts: Array<{ id, title, createdAt }> }>
221: ```
222: 
223: **Reduce a to-many relation to a scalar.** A refinement callback may return a *reducer* — `count()`, `sum(field)`, `avg(field)`, `min(field)`, `max(field)`, plus the lossless `countBigInt()`, `sumBigInt(field)`, and `avgDecimal(field)` — instead of a collection. The parent's relation field then carries that one value rather than an array. Reducers exist only inside an `include(...)` callback; calling one elsewhere throws.
224: 
225: ```typescript
226: await db.orm.public.User.include('posts', (posts) => posts.count()).all();
227: // → Array<{ ...user, posts: number }> — a parent with no posts reads 0
228: 
229: await db.orm.public.User.include('posts', (posts) => posts.sum('views')).all();
230: // → Array<{ ...user, posts: number | null }>
231: 
232: await db.orm.public.User.include('posts', (posts) => posts.avg('views')).all();
233: // → Array<{ ...user, posts: number | null }>
234: 
235: await db.orm.public.User.include('posts', (posts) => posts.min('views')).all();
236: await db.orm.public.User.include('posts', (posts) => posts.max('views')).all();
237: // → Array<{ ...user, posts: number | null }>
238: 
239: // The lossless form, for a total that may outgrow a JS number:
240: await db.orm.public.User.include('posts', (posts) => posts.sumBigInt('views')).all();
241: // → Array<{ ...user, posts: bigint | null }>
242: 
243: // Several sub-views of one relation at once:
244: await db.orm.public.User.include('posts', (posts) =>
245:   posts.combine({ recent: posts.limit(3), total: posts.count() }),
246: ).all();
247: // → Array<{ ...user, posts: { recent: Post[]; total: number } }>
248: ```

288: ## Workflow — Aggregates
289: 
290: ```typescript
291: const totals = await db.orm.public.User.aggregate((aggregate) => ({
292:   totalUsers: aggregate.count(),
293: }));
294: 
295: const adminTotals = await db.orm.public.User
296:   .where({ kind: 'admin' })
297:   .aggregate((aggregate) => ({
298:     adminUsers: aggregate.count(),
299:   }));
300: 
301: // Group-by + aggregate.
302: const byKind = await db.orm.public.User
303:   .groupBy('kind')
304:   .having((having) => having.count().gte(minUsers))
305:   .aggregate((aggregate) => ({
306:     totalUsers: aggregate.count(),
307:   }));
308: ```
309: 
310: `aggregate` exposes `.count()`, `.sum(field)`, `.avg(field)`, `.min(field)`, `.max(field)`, and the lossless `.countBigInt()`, `.sumBigInt(field)`, `.avgDecimal(field)`. Project the aggregates into named result keys; the result type narrows accordingly.
311: 
312: **The bare operations answer as JS numbers. The suffixed ones answer losslessly.** An aggregate's type is the one its target declares and its nullability matches SQL semantics, both read from the contract. On PostgreSQL:
313: 
314: | Aggregate | Type | Empty result |
315: | --- | --- | --- |
316: | `count()` | `number` | `0` |
317: | `countBigInt()` | `bigint` | `0n` |
318: | `sum(field)` over `int2` / `int4` / `int8` / `BigIntNumber` | `number \| null` | `null` (SQL `SUM` over zero rows is `NULL`) |
319: | `sumBigInt(field)` over any integer | `bigint \| null` | `null` |
320: | `sum(field)` over `float4` / `float8` | `number \| null` | `null` |
321: | `sum(field)` over `numeric` | decimal `string \| null` | `null` |
322: | `sum(field)` over `UnboundedInt` | `bigint \| null` — that column's own family | `null` |
323: | `avg(field)` over any integer | `number \| null` | `null` |
324: | `avgDecimal(field)` over any integer or `numeric` | decimal `string \| null` | `null` |
325: | `avg(field)` over a float | `number \| null` | `null` |
326: | `min(field)` / `max(field)` | the column's own type `\| null` — `text` where the column is `varchar` | `null` |
327: 
328: **`count()`, and `sum` over an integer column, throw outside ±(2^53 − 1) — they never round.** Those two are the results a guarded integer codec produces. The rows above the guard does not reach: `sum` over `numeric`, `UnboundedInt`, or a float column, and every `avg`, which is a fraction already. The error is `RUNTIME.DECODE_FAILED` (`… value must be an integer within the safe integer range, got …`), and it fires on the include path too. That is the trade the defaults make: a `number` you can compare, serialise, and do arithmetic with, and a loud failure instead of a quietly wrong total. Switch that one call to `sumBigInt` / `countBigInt` where the magnitude is real.
329: 
330: **Float and Decimal columns keep their own family.** `sum` over `numeric` is still a decimal string, and `sum` over `float8` still a `number` — the defaults policy is about integers, and a column whose author chose `numeric` already chose its representation.
331: 
332: **SQLite states the same policy.** `count`, `sum` over integers, and `avg` all read as `number`; `countBigInt` and `sumBigInt` are there too. There is no `avgDecimal` — SQLite has no exact decimal type, so the method does not exist on a SQLite contract.

# Plan — Módulo CRM / Clientes (CRUD + búsqueda en tiempo real)

Verifiqué primero la API real de Prisma 8 en este repo (guía `prisma-8`): sí soporta `ilike`, `or()`, `orderBy`, `limit/offset` y `aggregate(count())` — el plan no asume nada que no exista. **No requiere migración**: `Customer` ya tiene `name, email, phone, active, createdAt` y `tenantId`.

## 1. Decisiones de arquitectura

| Tema | Decisión | Por qué |
|---|---|---|
| Mutaciones | **Server Actions** (`createCustomerAction`, `updateCustomerAction`, `archiveCustomerAction`) | Spec lo pide; sin libs nuevas (`useActionState` + `useFormStatus` de React 19) |
| "Tiempo real" | **URL como fuente de verdad**: input → debounce 250 ms → `router.replace("?q=...")` → RSC relee `searchParams` → refetch | Resultados al escribir sin botón "Buscar"; back/forward y links compartibles funcionan; sin websockets ni react-query |
| Filtros | `?q=&status=active|archived&sort=&page=` leídos en `page.tsx` (Server) | Todo renderizado en servidor; el cliente solo toca la URL |
| Acceso a datos | Siempre vía `tenantDb` (ya inyecta `tenantId`) | Aislamiento multi-tenant por construcción |
| Seguridad | Cada action re-valida servidor: `auth()` → membership en el tenant (nunca confiar en el form) | Las actions son endpoints públicos |
| Borrar | **Archivar** (`active=false`) | `Payment.customerId` haría `SetNull` al borrar duro → perderías histórico de cobros |

## 2. Estructura de carpetas

```
app/[tenant]/crm/
├── page.tsx                      ← RSC: lee searchParams, consulta BD, renderiza toolbar + tabla
├── loading.tsx                   ← skeleton de tabla mientras resuelve el refetch
├── actions.ts                    ← createCustomerAction / updateCustomerAction / archiveCustomerAction / restore
├── validators.ts                 ← validación a mano de name/email/phone (sin zod)
└── _components/                  ← privado: no genera ruta
    ├── customer-search.tsx       ← client: input + debounce 250ms + useTransition
    ├── customer-filters.tsx      ← client: estado (activos/archivados) + orden
    ├── customer-toolbar.tsx      ← envuelve search+filters+botón "Nuevo cliente"
    ├── customer-table.tsx        ← client: tabla desktop / tarjetas mobile + acciones por fila
    ├── customer-form.tsx         ← client: crear/editar (modal) con useActionState
    └── delete-customer-dialog.tsx← client: confirmación de archivar

lib/tenant-db.ts                  ← AMPLIAR (ya existe):
    customers.search({q, status, sort, limit, offset}) → {rows, total}
    customers.archive(id) / customers.restore(id)
```

Los componentes de shell de Fase 2 quedan en `app/components/tenant/`; los del módulo van en `_components/` junto a su ruta (no se mezclan).

## 3. Capa de datos (`lib/tenant-db.ts`)

```ts
search({ q, status, sort, page }) {
  const where = [tenant scoping]           // implícito en tenant-db
  if (q)     → or(c.name.ilike(%q%), c.email.ilike(%q%), c.phone.ilike(%q%))  // escapando % _ \
  if (status)→ c.active.eq(status === "active")
  rows  = db.orm...where(...).orderBy(sort).limit(20).offset((page-1)*20).all()
  total = db.orm...where(...).aggregate(a => ({ total: a.count() }))
}
```

## 4. Server Actions (`actions.ts`)

Flujo de cada una: `auth()` → userId → `tenantDb` desde el `tenantSlug` del form (hidden) → **verificar que el usuario es miembro** (`findByClerkUserId`) → validar campos (`validators.ts`) → operar → `revalidatePath("/{slug}/crm")` → devolver `{ok, errors, fieldValues}` para `useActionState`.

- `createCustomerAction` → `customers.create` (trim, email minúsculas, detectar duplicado informativo)
- `updateCustomerAction` → `customers.update(id, …)` (scoped `where({id, tenantId})` → imposible tocar otro tenant)
- `archiveCustomerAction` / `restoreCustomerAction` → `active: false | true`

## 5. UI de la tabla

- Columnas: Cliente (iniciales + nombre + email), Teléfono, Estado (badge), Creado, Acciones (✎ editar, 🗄 archivar).
- **Desktop**: tabla · **Mobile** (`sm:hidden`): tarjetas apiladas — consistente con Fase 2.
- Estados: `loading.tsx` skeleton · vacío "Aún no hay clientes" · sin resultados "Sin coincidencias para «x»".
- Orden: Recientes / Nombre A–Z / Nombre Z–A. Paginación: 20 por página con contador.
- Al cambiar `q` o filtros → `page=1`.

## 6. Orden de implementación

1. `lib/tenant-db.ts`: `customers.search` + `archive/restore`.
2. `validators.ts` + `actions.ts`.
3. `page.tsx` real (reemplaza `ModulePlaceholder`) + `loading.tsx`.
4. `_components/` (search → filters → table → form → dialog).
5. Verificación: `tsc` + `eslint` + `build` + prueba manual (crear, editar, archivar, buscar, filtrar, paginar) + revisar aislamiento con 2 tenants.

**No se toca**: `contract.prisma`, `proxy.ts`, config de Clerk.

2. **Crear/editar** → ¿modal sobre la tabla o ruta `/crm/customers/new`? *(modal — conserva búsqueda y filtros)*
3. **Listado** → ¿paginación de 20 o todos de una? *(paginación de 20)*

---

### 🎯 Puntos Fuertes Destacados

1. **Búsqueda basada en la URL (** **searchParams** **\+** **useTransition** **)**:
  * Es el patrón canónico en App Router. Mantener el estado en la URL como fuente de verdad hace que las búsquedas sean **compartibles, navegables por el historial del navegador (back/forward)** y no requieran bibliotecas externas de estado.
2. **Soft Delete / Archivo (** **active: false** **)**:
  * **Decisión crítica de diseño de base de datos.** Si eliminaras un registro de `Customer` de forma dura (*hard delete*), romperías la integridad referencial con sus cobros (`Payment`), pedidos (`Order`) y membresías (`Membership`), o dejarías huérfanos registros financieros.
3. **Seguridad Zero-Trust en Server Actions**:
  * Re-validar `auth()` y la pertenencia del usuario al `tenantId` directamente en las Server Actions previene vulnerabilidades de modificación de parámetros desde el cliente.
4. **Organización con Carpetas Privadas (** **\_components** **)**:
  * El uso del prefijo `_components` evita que Next.js interprete esa carpeta como un segmento de ruta, manteniendo el proyecto limpio y modular.

---

### 💡 3 Detalle Criteriales a Asegurar Durante la Implementación

1. **Sincronización del Schema en Prisma**:
  * Asegúrate de que el modelo `Customer` en tu `schema.prisma` tenga el campo `active Boolean @default(true)` o `archivedAt DateTime?`. Si no lo tiene, agregamos `active Boolean @default(true)` antes de ejecutar la migración.
2. **Invalidación de Caché (** **revalidatePath** **)**:
  * En cada Server Action (`createCustomerAction`, `updateCustomerAction`, `archiveCustomerAction`), asegúrate de llamar a `revalidatePath(`/${tenant}/crm`)` para que el React Server Component recargue los datos actualizados de PostgreSQL sin refrescar toda la página.
3. **UX Fluent con** **useTransition**:
  * Al actualizar la URL durante el debounce de búsqueda (250 ms), envolver la mutación de la URL en `startTransition` mantendrá el campo de texto respondiendo al instante sin congelar la escritura del usuario.

```tsx
"use client";
export default function CustomerSearch({ placeholder }: ...) {
  const router = useRouter();
  const pathname = usePathname(); // current path (careful: tenant path!)
  const searchParams = useSearchParams();
  const [value, setValue] = useState(searchParams.get("q") ?? "");
  const [, startTransition] = useTransition();
  const timerRef = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const next = value;
    const current = searchParams.get("q") ?? "";
    if (next === current) return;
    timerRef.current = setTimeout(() => {
      const params = new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString());
      if (next) params.set("q", next); else params.delete("q");
      params.delete("page"); // reset page
      startTransition(() => router.replace(`${pathname}?${params}`, { scroll: false }));
    }, 250);
    return () => clearTimeout(timerRef.current);
  }, [value]); // hmm deps: include searchParams? that would re-run on param change → could loop.
```
Careful about loops: effect on `value` only (plus refs for router/pathname/searchParams to avoid stale closure — but including them in deps triggers re-run when URL changes → then `next === current` check returns early ✓ no loop).

Actually: when URL updates from our own replace, `searchParams` changes → effect re-runs → value===current → return ✓. Safe.

customers: {
  ...existing methods...
  
  search: async ({ q, status = "active", sort = "recent", page = 1, pageSize = 20 }) => {
    const text = (q ?? "").trim();
    const pattern = `%${text.replace(/[\\%_]/g, (ch) => `\\${ch}`)}%`;

    let collection = db.orm.public.Customer
      .where({ tenantId })
      .where((c) => c.active.eq(status === "active"));

    if (text) {
      collection = collection.where((c) =>
        or(c.name.ilike(pattern), c.email.ilike(pattern), c.phone.ilike(pattern)),
      );
    }

    const ordered =
      sort === "name_asc"
        ? collection.orderBy((c) => c.name.asc())
        : sort === "name_desc"
          ? collection.orderBy((c) => c.name.desc())
          : collection.orderBy((c) => c.createdAt.desc());

    const [rows, agg] = await Promise.all([
      ordered.limit(pageSize).offset((page - 1) * pageSize).all(),
      collection.aggregate((a) => ({ total: a.count() })),
    ]);

    return { rows, total: agg.total };
  },
```

.claude/skills/prisma-8/references/queries-postgres.md:353:The concept: `db.sql.<ns>.<table>` is a table-shaped builder that produces a *plan*. The plan is a serialisable description of the query (AST + parameters); you run it through the runtime. Pick the runtime method by the result the plan declares: `db.runtime().query(plan)` for rows (it returns the same `AsyncIterableResult` as `.all()`, so `await` it for an array), `db.runtime().execute(plan)` for a write with no `RETURNING` (it resolves `{ affectedRows }` and returns no rows). The builder gives you the lanes the ORM doesn't express — explicit `JOIN`, arbitrary expression projection, target-specific operations through extension helpers — without dropping to raw SQL.

export type CustomerFormValues = { name: string; email: string; phone: string };
export type CustomerFieldErrors = Partial<Record<keyof CustomerFormValues, string>>;

export type CustomerValidation =
  | { ok: true; values: CustomerFormValues }
  | { ok: false; errors: CustomerFieldErrors; values: CustomerFormValues };

const EMAIL_RE = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]{2,}$/;
const PHONE_RE = /^\+?[0-9\s\-().]{5,20}$/;

export function validateCustomer(formData: FormData): CustomerValidation {
  const values = {
    name: String(formData.get("name") ?? "").trim(),
    email: String(formData.get("email") ?? "").trim().toLowerCase(),
    phone: String(formData.get("phone") ?? "").trim(),
  };
  const errors: CustomerFieldErrors = {};
  if (values.name.length < 2) errors.name = "Ingresa al menos 2 caracteres.";
  else if (values.name.length > 120) errors.name = "Máximo 120 caracteres.";
  if (values.email && !EMAIL_RE.test(values.email)) errors.email = "Ingresa un correo válido.";
  else if (values.email.length > 200) ...
  if (values.phone && !PHONE_RE.test(values.phone)) errors.phone = "Teléfono no válido (solo dígitos, espacios, +, -, ., ().";
  return Object.keys(errors).length ? {ok:false, errors, values} : {ok:true, values};
}

"use client";
import { usePathname, useRouter, useSearchParams } from "next/navigation";
import { Search, X } from "lucide-react";
import { useEffect, useRef, useState, useTransition } from "react";

const DEBOUNCE_MS = 250;

export default function CustomerSearch() {
  const router = useRouter();
  const pathname = usePathname();
  const searchParams = useSearchParams();
  const [value, setValue] = useState(() => searchParams.get("q") ?? "");
  const [, startTransition] = useTransition();
  const timerRef = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null);

  const paramQ = searchParams.get("q") ?? "";

  // Sincroniza cuando la URL cambia desde fuera (back/forward, filtros).
  useEffect(() => { setValue(paramQ); }, [paramQ]);

  // Debounce → actualiza la URL (la página RSC relee searchParams).
  useEffect(() => {
    if (value === paramQ) return;
    if (timerRef.current) clearTimeout(timerRef.current);
    timerRef.current = setTimeout(() => {
      const params = new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString());
      const next = value.trim();
      if (next) params.set("q", next); else params.delete("q");
      params.delete("page");
      startTransition(() => {
        router.replace(`${pathname}?${params.toString()}`, { scroll: false });
      });
    }, DEBOUNCE_MS);
    return () => { if (timerRef.current) clearTimeout(timerRef.current); };
  }, [value, paramQ, searchParams, pathname, router, startTransition]);
```
Hmm — including `searchParams` in deps: when URL changes → effect reruns → value===paramQ → early return BUT before that the cleanup clears pending timer... Sequence: user types "ab" → effect runs (value="ab", paramQ="") → timer set. User waits → timer fires → router.replace → searchParams updates → effect cleanup (clear timer — already fired) + rerun → value "ab" vs paramQ "ab" → return ✓.

But danger: if user types "abc" while first timer pending: value change → cleanup clears timer → new timer ✓.

Danger case: paramQ effect (`setValue(paramQ)`) runs when URL changes — after our replace, paramQ === value ✓ no-op.

Race: user types "abc", timer fires → replace with q=abc. Before URL resolves, user types "abcd": value="abcd", effect (deps changed: value) → clears? Timer already fired (no pending) → sets new timer for "abcd". URL then updates to q=abc → paramQ effect: setValue("abc") ← **OVERWRITES user's "abcd"!** ✗ That's a real bug (input jumps back).

Mitigation: only sync from paramQ when input is not focused? Use a ref tracking focus:
```tsx
const focusedRef = useRef(false);
onFocus → true, onBlur → false
useEffect(() => { if (!focusedRef.current) setValue(paramQ); }, [paramQ]);
```
That avoids clobbering during typing ✓ and still syncs on back/forward when unfocused ✓. 

Also the debounce effect comparing `value === paramQ` — during typing "abcd" while URL says "abc": value≠paramQ → schedules timer for "abcd" ✓ fine.

Edge: while focused and URL changes externally (back button) — rare; ignore ✓.

Hmm: `new Date(String(Temporal.Instant))` — if String gives "2026-10-07T14:44:12.123456789Z" → does JS parse? V8 accepts ≥3 fractional digits and I *believe* arbitrary precision... Let me think: ES spec date time string format allows only 3 fractional digits (SSS). V8 historically is lenient (parses more digits) — but ES spec says implementations may accept non-conforming strings. V8: `Date.parse("2026-10-07T14:44:12.123456789Z")` → returns valid timestamp (I'm ~90% sure V8 accepts it). Risk if not: empty date shown.

Safer: normalize first:
```ts
function toDate(value: unknown): Date | null {
  if (value instanceof Date) return value;
  const raw = String(value);
  // Trunca fracciones de segundo a milisegundos (Temporal.Instant → ISO con nanos)
  const iso = raw.replace(/\.(\d{3})\d*(Z|[+-])/, ".$1$2");
  const date = new Date(iso);
  return Number.isNaN(date.getTime()) ? null : date;
}
```
Hmm — Temporal.Instant.toString() format: "2026-10-07T14:44:12.123456789Z" ✓ regex `\.(\d{3})\d*(Z|[+-])` → ".123Z" ✓. If no fraction ".123Z"→ `\.(\d{3})\d*` requires at least 3 digits ✓ (Temporal always prints0, 3, 6, or 9 digits — could be ".123Z" ✓ or "2026-10-07T14:44:12Z" (no fraction) → regex doesn't match → parse as-is ✓ valid.

Also could be Temporal with offset "+00:00"? Instant.toString() always Z ✓.

Edge: paramQ changes after our replace → effect [paramQ] runs: document.activeElement — after replace, the input likely still focused → skip setValue ✓ (value already equals new paramQ anyway since we typed it... unless trim differs). E.g. user types "ana " → value="ana " vs paramQ="ana" (trimmed by URL set) → value !== paramQ → schedules another timer → sets same URL → infinite-ish loop? Let's trace: value="ana ", timer → params q="ana" → replace → paramQ="ana". Effect [value] deps: value unchanged since schedule → no re-run. paramQ effect: activeElement is input → skip. So value stays "ana ", paramQ "ana" — no loop, but the effect [value] won't reschedule because deps didn't change... wait, effect [value] ran when value became "ana " (scheduling timer). After timer fired, no dependency changed → effect doesn't re-run → no loop ✓. 

But later: user types "ana" again (removes space) → value "ana" === paramQ → effect returns early ✓ fine.

Trailing-space loop risk: if something else triggers effect [value] re-run while value="ana " and paramQ="ana"... deps only [value] — value unchanged → no rerun ✓ safe. On unmount cleanup ✓.

Also leading/trailing space in display value kept until URL updates ✓ fine.

Hmm, one more: `searchParams` used inside effect but not in deps (eslint-disable added) ✓ intentional to avoid rescheduling loops.

import { notFound } from "next/navigation";
import { db } from "@/prisma/db";
import { createTenantDb } from "@/lib/tenant-db";
import CustomerToolbar from "./_components/customer-toolbar";
import CustomerTable, { type CustomerRow } from "./_components/customer-table";
import type { CustomerSort, CustomerStatus } from "./_components/customer-filters";

const PAGE_SIZE = 20;

const dateFormatter = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("es-CO", {
  day: "2-digit", month: "short", year: "numeric", timeZone: "America/Bogota",
});

function toDate(value: unknown): Date | null {
  if (value instanceof Date) return value;
  const raw = String(value);
  // Temporal.Instant → ISO con fracciones de nanos: JS Date solo acepta ms.
  const iso = raw.replace(/\.(\d{3})\d*(Z|[+-])/, ".$1$2");
  const date = new Date(iso);
  return Number.isNaN(date.getTime()) ? null : date;
}

import { db } from "./prisma/db";
import { createTenantDb } from "./lib/tenant-db";

async function main() {
  const tenant = await db.orm.public.Tenant.where({ active: true }).first();
  if (!tenant) { console.log("NO_TENANT"); return; }
  const t = createTenantDb(tenant.id);

  // Crear 3 clientes únicos
  const suffix = Date.now().toString().slice(-6);
  const names = [`Smoke Ada ${suffix}`, `Smoke Bob ${suffix}`, `Smoke Cir ${suffix}`];
  for (const n of names) { await t.customers.create({ name: n, email: `${suffix}@smoke.dev`, phone: "+57 300 000 0000", active: true }); }
  console.log("created", names.length);

  // search con q
  const { rows, total } = await t.customers.search({ q: `Smoke ${suffix}`, status: "active", sort: "name_asc", page: 1, pageSize: 20 });
  console.log("search q:", total, rows.length, rows.map(r => r.name).join(", "));

  // search por email
  const { total: tEmail } = await t.customers.search({ q: suffix + "@smoke.dev", status: "active", sort: "recent" });
  console.log("search email:", tEmail);

  // archivar uno
  const [toArchive, ...rest] = rows;
  await t.customers.archive(toArchive.id);
  console.log("archived:", toArchive.name);

  // search archivados
  const { total: archivedTotal } = await t.customers.search({ q: suffix, status: "archived" });
  console.log("archived total:", archivedTotal);

  // restore
  await t.customers.restore(toArchive.id);
  console.log("restored");

  // archivar dos y deleteManyArchived
  const targets = rows.slice(0, 2);
  for (const c of targets) await t.customers.archive(c.id);
  const deleted = await t.customers.deleteManyArchived(targets.map(c => c.id));
  console.log("hard deleted:", deleted);

  // restore + verify count active
  const { total: totalActive } = await t.customers.search({ q: suffix, status: "active" });
  console.log("remaining active:", totalActive);

  // limpiar el tercero
  await t.customers.archive(rows[2].id);
  const cleaned = await t.customers.deleteManyArchived([rows[2].id]);
  console.log("cleanup deleted:", cleaned);
}

main().then(() => process.exit(0)).catch((e) => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); });
```

# 1. Contexto del proyecto

## Arquitectura Multi-Tenant

NEXUS THRIVE utiliza una arquitectura Multi-Tenant.

Cada registro de negocio pertenece obligatoriamente a un `tenantId`.

Todo acceso a datos debe realizarse utilizando el contexto/capa de datos del tenant:

```text
tenantDb
```

Nunca se debe consultar información de otro tenant.

Todas las queries deben estar estrictamente aisladas mediante:

```text
tenantId
```

No confiar únicamente en valores enviados desde el cliente.

El `tenantId` debe resolverse desde el contexto autenticado y validado del tenant.

---

## Stack

* Next.js App Router
* React 19
* TypeScript
* Prisma ORM
* PostgreSQL
* Tailwind CSS
* Clerk Auth
* Server Components
* Server Actions
* `useActionState`

---

# 2. Modelos relevantes

## Payment

El modelo representa los ingresos/cobros:

```text
Payment
├── id
├── tenantId
├── customerId
├── amount
├── method
├── status
├── reference
├── date
└── createdAt
```

Estados:

```text
paid
pending
failed
```

Métodos:

```text
nequi
efectivo
tarjeta
wompi
```

---

## Expense

Representa los gastos de caja menor:

```text
Expense
├── id
├── tenantId
├── description
├── amount
├── category
├── date
└── createdAt
```

---

## Customer

Representa los clientes del negocio:

```text
Customer
├── id
├── name
├── email
├── phone
└── active
```

---

# 3. Capa de datos

Archivo principal:

```text
lib/tenant-db.ts
```

o, si la arquitectura existente lo requiere:

```text
lib/tenant/
└── repositories/
    └── finance.ts
```

No dupliques innecesariamente la lógica existente.

## Implementar `finance.getMetrics()`

Crear:

```text
finance.getMetrics({
  tenantId,
  month,
  year
})
```

Debe calcular en servidor:

### Total de ingresos

Sumar únicamente los pagos:

```text
status = paid
```

dentro del mes y año solicitado.

```text
Total Ingresos = SUM(Payment.amount)
```

---

### Total de gastos

Sumar los gastos del mismo período:

```text
Total Gastos = SUM(Expense.amount)
```

---

### Balance neto

```text
Balance Neto = Total Ingresos - Total Gastos
```

---

### Métodos de pago

Generar un desglose de ingresos agrupado por método:

```text
Efectivo
Nequi
Tarjeta
Wompi
```

La agrupación debe realizarse en servidor.

No descargar todos los pagos al cliente para realizar los cálculos.

---

Implementar:

```text
finance.listPayments({
  tenantId,
  q,
  method,
  status,
  page,
  limit
})
```

Debe permitir:

* Búsqueda
* Filtro por método
* Filtro por estado

* Ordenamiento por fecha

Debe incluir la relación con `Customer`.

Mostrar como mínimo:

```text
customer.name
customer.email
```

La consulta debe continuar estando aislada por:

tenantId
```

# 6. Server Actions

Crear:

```text
app/[tenant]/finance/actions.ts
```

Las Server Actions deben ejecutarse exclusivamente en servidor.

Utilizar:

```tsx
"use server";
```

---

## `createPaymentAction`

Debe:

1. Validar autenticación.
2. Resolver el tenant actual.
3. Validar que el usuario tenga acceso al tenant.
4. Validar el `customerId`.
5. Confirmar que el cliente pertenece al mismo tenant.
6. Validar que el monto sea positivo.
7. Validar el método de pago.
8. Validar los demás campos necesarios.
9. Crear el registro `Payment`.
10. Revalidar:

```text
/[tenant]/finance
/[tenant]
```

Utilizar:

```tsx
revalidatePath(...)
```

No confiar en `tenantId` enviado desde el formulario.

---

## `createExpenseAction`

Debe:

1. Validar autenticación.
2. Resolver el tenant actual.
3. Validar acceso al tenant.
4. Validar descripción.
5. Validar categoría.
6. Validar que el monto sea positivo.
7. Crear el registro `Expense`.
8. Revalidar:

```text
/[tenant]/finance
/[tenant]
```

Las categorías disponibles inicialmente serán:

```text
Servicios
Nómina
Insumos
Arriendo
Otros
```

---

Implementa validación robusta tanto para formularios como para Server Actions.

Nunca confíes únicamente en:

* `required`
* validaciones HTML
* validaciones del cliente

La validación importante debe ejecutarse en servidor.

Validar como mínimo:

### Payment

```text
customerId
amount > 0
method válido
status válido si corresponde
reference opcional
```

### Expense

```text
description
category válida
amount > 0
```

Evitar aceptar valores arbitrarios enviados manualmente desde el cliente.

No mezclar datos de otros tenants.

# 16. Manejo de dinero

Los campos monetarios de Prisma utilizan:

```text
Decimal
```

No pasar objetos `Decimal` directamente a Client Components.

Antes de cruzar el límite Server → Client, transformar los valores a tipos serializables:

```text
number
```

o:

```text
string
```

según corresponda.

No utilizar conversiones inseguras que puedan producir errores de precisión innecesarios.

Todo valor monetario mostrado en la interfaz debe utilizar:

```text
es-CO
```

y:

```text
COP
```

Ejemplo conceptual:

```text
$ 250.000
```

Utilizar `Intl.NumberFormat` para el formateo.

Crear una utilidad reutilizable si es necesario:

```text
formatCurrency()
```

No repetir manualmente la lógica de formato por toda la aplicación.

# 18. Seguridad Multi-Tenant

Esta es una prioridad absoluta.

Nunca debe ser posible:

```text
Tenant A → consultar datos de Tenant B
```

Todas las consultas deben incluir obligatoriamente el tenant correspondiente.

Ejemplo conceptual:

```text
Payment.where({
  tenantId,
  ...
})
```

No confiar en:

```text
tenantId
```

proporcionado directamente por el navegador.

El tenant debe derivarse del contexto/ruta autenticada y validarse contra la base de datos.

Los `customerId` utilizados para crear pagos también deben comprobarse contra el tenant actual.

@/prisma/db

y acceder a PostgreSQL.

Solo deben encargarse de:

No deben importar:

@clerk/nextjs/server
@/prisma/db

ni módulos `server-only`.

# 1. Contexto del proyecto

## Arquitectura Multi-Tenant

NEXUS THRIVE utiliza una arquitectura Multi-Tenant.

Cada registro de negocio pertenece obligatoriamente a un `tenantId`.

Todo acceso a datos debe realizarse utilizando el contexto/capa de datos del tenant:

```text
tenantDb
```

Nunca se debe consultar información de otro tenant.

Todas las queries deben estar estrictamente aisladas mediante:

```text
tenantId
```

No confiar únicamente en valores enviados desde el cliente.

El `tenantId` debe resolverse desde el contexto autenticado y validado del tenant.

---

## Stack

* Next.js App Router
* React 19
* TypeScript
* Prisma ORM
* PostgreSQL
* Tailwind CSS
* Clerk Auth
* Server Components
* Server Actions
* `useActionState`

---

# 2. Modelos relevantes

## Payment

El modelo representa los ingresos/cobros:

```text
Payment
├── id
├── tenantId
├── customerId
├── amount
├── method
├── status
├── reference
├── date
└── createdAt
```

Estados:

```text
paid
pending
failed
```

Métodos:

```text
nequi
efectivo
tarjeta
wompi
```

---

## Expense

Representa los gastos de caja menor:

```text
Expense
├── id
├── tenantId
├── description
├── amount
├── category
├── date
└── createdAt
```

---

## Customer

Representa los clientes del negocio:

```text
Customer
├── id
├── name
├── email
├── phone
└── active
```

Archivo principal:

```text
lib/tenant-db.ts
```

o, si la arquitectura existente lo requiere:

lib/tenant/
└── repositories/
    └── finance.ts
```

No dupliques innecesariamente la lógica existente.

## Implementar `finance.getMetrics()`

Crear:

```text
finance.getMetrics({
  tenantId,
  month,
  year
})
```

Debe calcular en servidor:

### Total de ingresos

Sumar únicamente los pagos:

```text
status = paid
```

dentro del mes y año solicitado.

```text
Total Ingresos = SUM(Payment.amount)
```

---

### Total de gastos

Sumar los gastos del mismo período:

```text
Total Gastos = SUM(Expense.amount)
```

---

### Balance neto

```text
Balance Neto = Total Ingresos - Total Gastos
```

---

### Métodos de pago

Generar un desglose de ingresos agrupado por método:

```text
Efectivo
Nequi
Tarjeta
Wompi
```

La agrupación debe realizarse en servidor.

No descargar todos los pagos al cliente para realizar los cálculos.

---

Implementar:

finance.listPayments({
  tenantId,
  q,
  method,
  status,
  page,
  limit
})

Debe permitir:

* Búsqueda
* Filtro por método
* Filtro por estado

Debe incluir la relación con `Customer`.

Mostrar como mínimo:

customer.name
customer.email

La consulta debe continuar estando aislada por:

tenantId
```

# 6. Server Actions

Crear:

```text
app/[tenant]/finance/actions.ts
```

Las Server Actions deben ejecutarse exclusivamente en servidor.

Utilizar:

```tsx
"use server";
```

---

## `createPaymentAction`

Debe:

1. Validar autenticación.
2. Resolver el tenant actual.
3. Validar que el usuario tenga acceso al tenant.
4. Validar el `customerId`.
5. Confirmar que el cliente pertenece al mismo tenant.
6. Validar que el monto sea positivo.
7. Validar el método de pago.
8. Validar los demás campos necesarios.
9. Crear el registro `Payment`.
10. Revalidar:

```text
/[tenant]/finance
/[tenant]
```

Utilizar:

```tsx
revalidatePath(...)
```

No confiar en `tenantId` enviado desde el formulario.

---

## `createExpenseAction`

Debe:

1. Validar autenticación.
2. Resolver el tenant actual.
3. Validar acceso al tenant.
4. Validar descripción.
5. Validar categoría.
6. Validar que el monto sea positivo.
7. Crear el registro `Expense`.
8. Revalidar:

```text
/[tenant]/finance
/[tenant]
```

Las categorías disponibles inicialmente serán:

```text
Servicios
Nómina
Insumos
Arriendo
Otros
```

---

# 7. Validación

Implementa validación robusta tanto para formularios como para Server Actions.

Nunca confíes únicamente en:

* `required`
* validaciones HTML
* validaciones del cliente

La validación importante debe ejecutarse en servidor.

Validar como mínimo:

### Payment

```text
customerId
amount > 0
method válido
status válido si corresponde
reference opcional
```

### Expense

```text
description
category válida
amount > 0
```

Evitar aceptar valores arbitrarios enviados manualmente desde el cliente.

26:| Postgres-specific feature (`LATERAL`, `FILTER`, custom aggregates) | **SQL builder**, falling back to extension operators when the extension provides them | DSL first; extensions can contribute operators (`postgis`, `pgvector`). |

30:The concept: `db.orm.<ns>.<Model>` returns a *collection* you compose method-by-method. Each call returns a new collection (immutable chaining); the terminal verb (`.all()` / `.first()` / `.aggregate(...)`) issues the query. There is no `.count()` terminal on the collection — `count()` is an `include` reducer and an `aggregate(...)` operation (both below). Predicates are lambdas over a field proxy: `u.field.<op>(value)`.

250:A reducer's result type is the one the target declares for that aggregate — the same types *Workflow — Aggregates* tabulates below, including the `null` a field-taking reducer answers for a parent with no related rows. The reducer set is read from the contract, so an operation a target or extension contributes shows up as a reducer under its own name, with no client change.

252-Nested `1:N → 1:N` includes (e.g. `User → posts → comments`) require the contract to advertise the `lateral` + `jsonAgg` capabilities for the active target. The Postgres adapter advertises both by default, so most apps get this for free; if the type system rejects a nested include with a *missing capability* error, route to `references/contract.md` to add the required capability declarations and use `references/queries.md` for query-shape guidance.

63:Operators on the field proxy include `.eq`, `.neq`, `.lt`, `.lte`, `.gt`, `.gte`, `.like`, `.ilike`, `.in([...])`, `.isNull()`, `.isNotNull()`. Extensions add target-specific operators on extension-typed columns (`pgvector`'s `.cosineDistance(...)`, `postgis`'s `.within(...)` / `.intersectsBbox(...)` / `.distanceSphere(...)`).
64-
65-**Full-text search** is built into the Postgres target, on any text column: `.fullTextMatches(q)` is the predicate, `.fullTextRank(q)` scores a row so you can order by relevance, and `.fullTextHeadline(q)` returns the text with `<b>` around the matches. The argument `q` is a `tsquery`, built with a helper from `@prisma/orm-postgres/target/full-text`. A bare string is a type error, because Postgres would read it as `tsquery` syntax without lowercasing or stemming it. Pick the helper by where the text comes from:
66-
67-- A search box: `websearchToTsquery(input)`. `"an exact phrase"`, `-excluded` and `or` work, and it never errors. `plaintoTsquery` requires every word; `phrasetoTsquery` requires the words in order.
68-- User input inside operator syntax, such as typeahead: the `tsquery` tag, `` tsquery`${term}:*` ``. The literal parts are trusted `tsquery` syntax you write. Each interpolated value becomes exactly one quoted term, so user input cannot add operators or break the syntax; an empty value adds no words, like a stop word. A value with several words becomes a phrase: `` tsquery`${'new y'}:*` `` gives `'new':* <-> 'y':*`, so the words must be adjacent and in order, and `:*` applies to each word. Do not put quotes around the interpolation yourself: `` tsquery`'${term}':*` `` is a syntax error for every input. Postgres `to_tsquery` then lowercases and stems every word. `` tsquery({ language: 'german' })`...` `` picks the configuration.
69-- Operator syntax you write in full: `toTsquery("'zebra' & !'graze'")`. Malformed text fails at execution, so never pass user input to it; use the `tsquery` tag for that.
--

136-The two forms emit the same SQL. Pick chained `.where()` when each clause adds a separate condition that reads as its own thought; pick `and(...)` when one logical predicate happens to have two parts and you want the visual grouping. Don't reach for a `between` helper — there isn't one.
137-
138-**Combinators** (`and`, `or`, `not`) compose predicates, and **relation predicates** (`.some(...)`, `.none(...)`, `.every(...)`) recurse into a relation. `.some()` and `.none()` take an optional predicate — `u.posts.none()` means "has no posts", `u.posts.some()` means "has at least one" — while `.every(...)` requires one: `u.posts.every((p) => p.published.eq(true))`. The combinators are exported from the façade's `orm-client` subpath:

310-`aggregate` exposes `.count()`, `.sum(field)`, `.avg(field)`, `.min(field)`, `.max(field)`, and the lossless `.countBigInt()`, `.sumBigInt(field)`, `.avgDecimal(field)`. Project the aggregates into named result keys; the result type narrows accordingly.
--
332-**SQLite states the same policy.** `count`, `sum` over integers, and `avg` all read as `number`; `countBigInt` and `sumBigInt` are there too. There is no `avgDecimal` — SQLite has no exact decimal type, so the method does not exist on a SQLite contract.
333-
334:**The ORM's `having(...)` stays a `number`.** Its comparand is typed `number` outright, whatever result type the aggregate carries, so `having.count().gte(minUsers)` takes a plain number — the value is inlined as a SQL literal and compared inside the database. Only the aggregate's *result*, the value that reaches your code, carries its target's type. The lossless variants are projection-only and have no HAVING method at all.
335-
336-**The SQL builder types its comparands differently.** `fns.gt(a, b)` types both operands from one codec, so a literal compared against an aggregate follows that aggregate's result codec — `fns.gt(fns.count(), 1)`, not `1n`. That applies in `having(...)`, in `where(...)`, and inside any larger expression.
337-
338-Nullability isn't a typing bug — it's faithful to what the database returns. Coalesce client-side when you want zero-fill:

listPayments: async ({ q, method, status, page = 1, limit = 10 }: PaymentListInput) => {
  const text = (q ?? "").trim();
  const pattern = `%${escapeLike(text)}%`;
  const safePage = Math.max(1, Math.trunc(page));
  const safeLimit = Math.min(100, Math.max(1, Math.trunc(limit)));

  let filtered = db.orm.public.Payment.where({ tenantId });
  if (status) filtered = filtered.where((p) => p.status.eq(status));
  if (method) filtered = filtered.where((p) => p.provider.eq(method));
  if (text) filtered = filtered.where((p) => or(p.description.ilike(pattern), p.providerRefId.ilike(pattern)));

  const [rows, { total }] = await Promise.all([
    filtered.orderBy((p) => p.createdAt.desc()).limit(safeLimit).offset((safePage - 1) * safeLimit).all(),
    filtered.aggregate((a) => ({ total: a.count() })),

  const customerById = new Map(customers.map((c) => [c.id, c]));
  ...
  return { rows: ..., total };
}

7: const DEBOUNCE_MS = 250;
8: 
9: /**
10:  * Buscador "en tiempo real": escribe → debounce 250 ms → actualiza `?q=` en
11:  * la URL → la página RSC relee `searchParams` y refresca. La URL es la única
12:  * fuente de verdad (back/forward y enlaces comparten el estado).
13:  */
14: export default function CustomerSearch() {
15:   const router = useRouter();
16:   const pathname = usePathname();
17:   const searchParams = useSearchParams();
18:   const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition();
19: 
20:   const paramQ = searchParams.get("q") ?? "";
21:   const [value, setValue] = useState(paramQ);
22: 
23:   // Evita que un cambio externo de la URL pise lo que el usuario está
24:   // escribiendo en este mismo momento (solo sincroniza sin foco).
25:   const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null);
26:   const timerRef = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null);
27: 
28:   useEffect(() => {
29:     if (document.activeElement !== inputRef.current) {
30:       setValue(paramQ);
31:     }
32:   }, [paramQ]);
33: 
34:   // Debounce → reemplaza la URL sin recargar (scroll intacto).
35:   useEffect(() => {
36:     if (value === paramQ) {
37:       return;
38:     }
39: 
40:     if (timerRef.current) {
41:       clearTimeout(timerRef.current);
42:     }
43: 
44:     timerRef.current = setTimeout(() => {
45:       const params = new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString());
46:       const next = value.trim();
47:       if (next) {
48:         params.set("q", next);
49:       } else {
50:         params.delete("q");
51:       }
52:       params.delete("page");
53:       startTransition(() => {
54:         router.replace(`${pathname}?${params.toString()}`, { scroll: false });
55:       });
56:     }, DEBOUNCE_MS);
57: 
58:     return () => {
59:       if (timerRef.current) {
60:         clearTimeout(timerRef.current);
61:       }
62:     };
63:     // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps

"use server";
import { auth } from "@clerk/nextjs/server";
import { revalidatePath } from "next/cache";
import { db } from "@/prisma/db";
import { createTenantDb } from "@/lib/tenant-db";
import { validatePayment, validateExpense, type PaymentFieldErrors, type ExpenseFieldErrors } from "./validators";

// requireTenantDb copiado

export async function createPaymentAction(prev, formData): Promise<PaymentFormState> {
  tenantSlug = formData.get("tenantSlug")
  // customerId opcional: "" → null
  const tenantDb = await requireTenantDb(tenantSlug);
  if (!tenantDb) return ACCESS_DENIED_PAYMENT;
  const validation = validatePayment(formData);
  if (!validation.ok) return { status: "error", errors: validation.errors, values: validation.values };
  // Si customerId dado → verificar pertenece al tenant
  if (validation.values.customerId) {
    const customer = await tenantDb.customers.get(validation.values.customerId);
    if (!customer) return { status: "error", message: "El cliente seleccionado no existe." };
  }
  await tenantDb.payments.create({...});
  revalidatePath(`/${tenantSlug}/finance`);
  revalidatePath(`/${tenantSlug}`);
  return { status: "ok" };
}

{
  "content": "\"use client\";\n\nimport { useTransition } from \"react\";\nimport { usePathname, useRouter, useSearchParams } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { ChevronLeft, ChevronRight, Loader2 } from \"lucide-react\";\n\n/**\n * Paginación genérica de Finanzas. Conserva el resto de los filtros de la\n * URL y solo cambia el parámetro de página de su sección (`ppage`/`gpage`).\n */\nexport default function PaginationLinks({\n  paramKey,\n  page,\n  totalPages,\n  totalLabel,\n}: {\n  paramKey: string;\n  page: number;\n  totalPages: number;\n  totalLabel: string;\n}) {\n  const router = useRouter();\n  const pathname = usePathname();\n  const searchParams = useSearchParams();\n  const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition();\n\n  const navigateToPage = (nextPage: number) => {\n    const params = new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString());\n    params.set(paramKey, String(nextPage));\n    startTransition(() => {\n      router.replace(`${pathname}?${params.toString()}`, { scroll: false });\n    });\n  };\n\n  if (totalPages <= 1) {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"flex flex-col items-center justify-between gap-3 sm:flex-row\">\n      <p className=\"text-xs text-slate-500\">\n        Página {page} de {totalPages} · {totalLabel}\n      </p>\n      <div className=\"flex items-center gap-2\">\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          disabled={page <= 1 || isPending}\n          onClick={() => navigateToPage(page - 1)}\n          className=\"inline-flex h-9 items-center gap-1 rounded-lg border border-slate-200 bg-white px-3 text-sm font-medium text-slate-700 transition hover:bg-slate-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50\"\n        >\n          <ChevronLeft aria-hidden=\"true\" className=\"h-4 w-4\" />\n          Anterior\n        </button>\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          disabled={page >= totalPages || isPending}\n          onClick={() => navigateToPage(page + 1)}\n          className=\"inline-flex h-9 items-center gap-1 rounded-lg border border-slate-200 bg-white px-3 text-sm font-medium text-slate-700 transition hover:bg-slate-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50\"\n        >\n          {isPending ? (\n            <Loader2 aria-hidden=\"true\" className=\"h-4 w-4 animate-spin\" />\n          ) : null}\n          Siguiente\n          <ChevronRight aria-hidden=\"true\" className=\"h-4 w-4\" />\n        </button>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n}",

Loader robusto:

```js
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { resolve, dirname, join } from 'node:path';

const ROOT = '/home/craxker/github/nexus-thrive';

export async function resolve(specifier, context, next) {
  // Alias @/ → <ROOT>/<path>.ts (o como viene)
  if (specifier.startsWith('@/')) {
    const candidates = [];
    const rel = specifier.slice(2);
    candidates.push(pathToFileURL(resolve(ROOT, rel)).href);
    if (!/\.[a-z]+($|\?)/i.test(rel)) {
      candidates.push(pathToFileURL(resolve(ROOT, rel + '.ts')).href);
    }
    for (const url of candidates) {
      const filePath = new URL(url).pathname;
      if ([url, url + '?x'].some(() => true) && existsSync(filePath)) return { url, shortCircuit: true };
    }
    return { url: candidates[0], shortCircuit: true };
  }
  // Relativos sin extensión: probar .ts / .d.ts (módulos del repo)
  if (specifier.startsWith('.') ) {
    const baseFile = context.parentURL ? new URL(context.parentURL).pathname : '';
    const base = dirname(baseFile);
    const target = resolve(base, specifier);
    for (const ext of ['.ts', '.d.ts', '.tsx', '/index.ts']) {
      if (existsSync(target + ext)) {
        return { url: pathToFileURL(target + ext).href, shortCircuit: true };
      }
    }
  }
  return next(specifier, context);
}
```
