Actividad reciente (mezcla ordenada)\n  // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n  const activity = await tenantDb.finance.getRecentActivity(5);\n  record(\"getRecentActivity trae 5\", activity.length === 5, `got ${activity.length}`);\n  const sorted = activity.every(\n    (item, index) => index === 0 || activity[index - 1].date >= item.date,\n  );\n  record(\"actividad ordenada desc por fecha\", sorted, activity.map((i) => `${i.type}:${i.date}`).join(\" | \"));\n  const expenseNegative = activity.find((item) => item.type === \"expense\");\n  record(\n    \"gastos con monto negativo\",\n    Boolean(expenseNegative && expenseNegative.amount < 0),\n    `got ${expenseNegative?.amount}`,\n  );\n  record(\n    \"payment rows empiezan con 'payment-' y expenses con 'expense-'\",\n    activity.every((item) => item.id.startsWith(item.type)),\n  );\n\n  // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n  // 8. Rango de mes: pago de OTRO mes no cuenta (si el modelo deja fijar fecha)\n  // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n  try {\n    const otherMonthYear = month === 1 ? year - 1 : year;\n    const otherMonth = month === 1 ? 12 : month - 1;\n    const outside = await db.orm.public.Payment.create(\n      {\n        tenantId: tenant.id,\n        customerId: null,\n        provider: \"CASH\",\n        status: \"APPROVED\",\n        amount: \"999999\",\n        description: \"Pago de otro mes\",\n        createdAt: new Date(Date.UTC(otherMonthYear, otherMonth - 1, 15, 5, 0, 0)).toISOString(),\n      } as never,\n    );\n    const metricsAgain = await tenantDb.finance.getMetrics({ month, year });\n    record(\n      \"pago de otro mes queda fuera del rango\",\n      metricsAgain.income === 150000,\n      `got ${metricsAgain.income} (pago ${toNumber(outside.amount)} excluido)`,\n    );\n  } catch (error) {\n    record(\"pago con createdAt manual\", false, `el modelo rechazó la fecha → ${error}`);\n  }\n\n  // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n  // 9. El codec de fechas de Prisma 8 (`timestamptz-temporal`) **exige `Temporal.Instant` en runtime** — tsc acepta strings pero el driver crashea. Lo resolví con rangos en `Temporal.Instant` y una declaración mínima en `lib/temporal.d.ts` (Node 26 trae el built-in; `@types/temporal` no existe en npm). Guardado en Engram.

No hice commit — avisame si querés que lo deje registrado.

# 1. CONTEXTO Y ARQUITECTURA

## Multi-Tenancy

NEXUS THRIVE utiliza una arquitectura Multi-Tenant.

Todo acceso a datos debe realizarse mediante `tenantDb`.

El `tenantId` debe ser obligatorio en todas las operaciones relacionadas con membresías.

Nunca se debe:

* consultar una membresía sin filtrar por `tenantId`;
* modificar una membresía perteneciente a otro tenant;
* obtener clientes de otro tenant;
* crear pagos asociados a otro tenant;
* confiar en un `tenantId` enviado directamente desde el cliente sin validación del contexto actual.

Flujo esperado:

```text
hostname
    ↓
proxy.ts
    ↓
tenant slug
    ↓
app/[tenant]
    ↓
TenantLayout
    ↓
tenantDb
    ↓
tenantId
    ↓
Membership / Customer / Payment
```

---

Utilizar:

```text
Next.js App Router
React 19
TypeScript
Prisma ORM 8

Server Actions
useActionState
```

Los componentes deben respetar correctamente la separación entre:

* Server Components

No convertir componentes Server en Client Components innecesariamente.

# 5. CÁLCULO DINÁMICO DEL ESTADO

El estado de una membresía debe calcularse dinámicamente utilizando `endDate`.

Reglas:

```text
active
→ faltan más de 3 días para vencer

expiring
→ faltan 3 días o menos para vencer

expired
→ endDate es anterior a la fecha/hora actual
```

Ejemplo conceptual:

```text
endDate > ahora + 3 días
→ active

ahora < endDate <= ahora + 3 días
→ expiring

endDate < ahora
→ expired
```

El cálculo debe realizarse utilizando fechas reales y no depender únicamente del valor persistido de `status`.

Si el estado persistido está desactualizado, el sistema debe mostrar el estado calculado correctamente.

---

# 6. ZONA HORARIA

La aplicación opera en Colombia.

Utilizar:

```text
America/Bogota
```

y formato:

```text
es-CO
```

La implementación debe respetar la naturaleza de las fechas de Prisma 8 y evitar conversiones incorrectas entre:

```text
Date
Temporal.Instant
UTC
America/Bogota
```

No convertir fechas arbitrariamente con `toISOString()` si eso puede alterar la fecha que debe visualizar el usuario.

La persistencia debe mantenerse consistente en UTC cuando corresponda, mientras que la presentación y las reglas de negocio deben considerar la zona horaria de Bogotá.

Evitar errores como:

```text
30/10/2026
```

mostrándose como:

```text
29/10/2026
```

por una conversión incorrecta de zona horaria.

# 10. `renewMembershipAction`

Crear:

```ts
renewMembershipAction
```

Debe permitir renovar una membresía:

```text
active
expiring
expired
```

La acción debe:

```text
/[tenant]
```

Si una membresía está vencida, la renovación debe comenzar desde la fecha actual o desde una fecha de negocio correctamente definida, evitando generar periodos ya vencidos.

```
# Skill: prisma-8

# Prisma 8 (Prisma 8)

> **Edit your data contract. Prisma handles the rest.**

Prisma 8 moves fast, and your training data about it is very likely outdated. This skill ships inside the installed Prisma packages, so it describes the exact version this project has — treat it and its reference files as the source of truth, over anything you remember about Prisma.

## Pre-conditions

Check these before acting on anything below. Halt on the first one that fails and tell the user what is missing.

1. **The project is on Prisma 8.** `prisma.config.ts` exports `definePrismaConfig({ orm: ... })`, and `package.json` depends on `@prisma/orm-postgres`, `@prisma/orm-sqlite`, or `@prisma/orm-mongo`. A project with `schema.prisma` and `@prisma/client` is Prisma 7 or earlier; this skill does not apply to it, and its instructions will break such a project.
2. **The skill matches the installed version.** Compare `metadata.library_version` in this file's frontmatter with the installed `@prisma/orm-*` version in `package.json`. If they differ, run `prisma skills sync` and re-read this file before continuing.
3. **The contract artefacts exist.** `contract.json` and `contract.d.ts` sit next to the contract source named by `prisma.config.ts`. If they are missing or older than the source, run `prisma contract emit` first; every query and migration instruction below assumes current artefacts.

**Import paths in the references.** The reference files spell façade imports as `@internal/<target>/<subpath>` and `@internal/extension-<name>/<subpath>`. In an application those packages are published as `@prisma/orm-<target>/<subpath>` (`@prisma/orm-postgres/runtime`, `@prisma/orm-mongo/config`, `@prisma/orm-sqlite/runtime`) and `@prisma/orm-extension-<name>/<subpath>` (`@prisma/orm-extension-pgvector/control`). Write the `@prisma/orm-*` name in user code; the two spellings are the same package. Paths already written as `@prisma/orm-*` in the references are exact. The `metadata.library_version` in this file's frontmatter is the version it was published with; if it does not match the project's installed Prisma packages, run `prisma skills sync` and re-read.

Prisma 8 is a contract-first data layer. This skill routes every Prisma 8 task to the right reference file — open the reference before writing code; do not answer from this file alone.

## The canonical model (one paragraph)

You author a **data contract** (a `contract.prisma` file, or a TypeScript builder). The framework emits machine-readable artifacts (`contract.json`, `contract.d.ts`) and gives you two runtime surfaces on SQL targets: a typed SQL query builder (`db.sql.<ns>.<table>`) and a typed ORM client (`db.orm.<ns>.<Model>`). On MongoDB targets only the ORM lane exists, and its keys are collection storage names (`db.orm.users`) rather than PSL model names — [`references/queries.md`](references/queries.md) § *MongoDB ORM addressing* covers the rule. Migrations are planned from the contract diff; you review them, optionally edit the `migration.ts` for data transforms, and apply.

Three steps the user does:

1. **Edit your data contract.** ([`references/contract.md`](references/contract.md))
2. **The system plans the migrations for you.** ([`references/migrations.md`](references/migrations.md))
3. **If you need data migrations, you edit `migration.ts` and execute it.** ([`references/migrations.md`](references/migrations.md))

Everything else — queries, runtime wiring, build integration, debugging, feedback — sits on top of those three.

One cross-cutting migration fact: `migration plan` does **not** chain from the newest migration on disk. Its origin is `--from`, else the `db` ref, else an empty database — so a project with no ref keeps planning from scratch. Over existing migrations the CLI refuses that (`MIGRATION.PLAN_ORIGIN_UNKNOWN`) instead of writing a full-create package; choose the exit that matches your intent rather than reflexively passing `--from @empty`. [`references/migration-model.md`](references/migration-model.md) § *The trap* explains which to choose.

## Routing rules

If the task clearly matches a row, open that reference directly without asking.

For a vague prompt, ask **one** disambiguating question. Pick from:

- *"Are you new to Prisma 8 and asking what you can do with it, or where to start?"* → [`references/quickstart.md`](references/quickstart.md) (first-touch orientation path).
- *"Do you want to set up a new Prisma 8 project, or wire it into an existing database?"* → [`references/quickstart.md`](references/quickstart.md).
- *"Do you want to edit your data contract (add a model / field / relation), or work with the database (migrations, queries)?"* → [`references/contract.md`](references/contract.md) vs the others.
- *"Is this about authoring a migration, or about reviewing what's going to run on deploy?"* → [`references/migrations.md`](references/migrations.md) vs [`references/migration-review.md`](references/migration-review.md). If it's about where a plan starts, refs, or an unexpected from-scratch plan → [`references/migration-model.md`](references/migration-model.md).
- *"Is this about wiring Prisma 8 into your build tool (Vite / Next.js / …), or about wiring `db.ts` and middleware at runtime?"* → [`references/build.md`](references/build.md) vs [`references/runtime.md`](references/runtime.md).
- *"What error or symptom are you seeing?"* → [`references/debug.md`](references/debug.md).
- *"Do you want to report this as a bug to the Prisma 8 team, or is this a feature request?"* → [`references/feedback.md`](references/feedback.md).
- *"Is the project you want to upgrade an application, or a Prisma extension package?"* → [`references/upgrade-app.md`](references/upgrade-app.md) vs [`references/upgrade-extension.md`](references/upgrade-extension.md).

If you still can't tell which reference applies, ask the user what they want to do. Do not guess.
```

```
  .where((s) => s.day.gte(start))
  .where((s) => s.day.lte(end))
  .all();

// Equivalent with an explicit `and(...)` inside one clause.
import { and } from '@prisma/orm-postgres/orm-client';
await db.orm.public.Sale
  .where((s) => and(s.day.gte(start), s.day.lte(end)))
  .all();
```

The two forms emit the same SQL. Pick chained `.where()` when each clause adds a separate condition that reads as its own thought; pick `and(...)` when one logical predicate happens to have two parts and you want the visual grouping. Don't reach for a `between` helper — there isn't one.

**Combinators** (`and`, `or`, `not`) compose predicates, and **relation predicates** (`.some(...)`, `.none(...)`, `.every(...)`) recurse into a relation. `.some()` and `.none()` take an optional predicate — `u.posts.none()` means "has no posts", `u.posts.some()` means "has at least one" — while `.every(...)` requires one: `u.posts.every((p) => p.published.eq(true))`. The combinators are exported from the façade's `orm-client` subpath:

```typescript
import { and, or, not } from '@prisma/orm-postgres/orm-client';

await db.orm.public.User
  .where((u) =>
    and(
      or(u.kind.eq('admin'), u.email.ilike('%@example.com')),
      not(u.posts.none((p) => p.title.ilike('%draft%'))),
    ),
  )
  .all();
```

**Sorting and pagination.** `.orderBy(...)` accepts a single lambda or an array of lambdas. Each calls `.asc()` / `.desc()` on a field, an extension-operation result, a to-one relation's field, or a to-many relation's `count(...)`. Every `.asc()` / `.desc()` takes `{ nulls: 'first' | 'last' }`. `.limit(n)` limits; `.offset(n)` offsets.

```typescript
await db.orm.public.Post
  .where((p) => p.authorId.eq(userId))
  .orderBy([(p) => p.createdAt.desc(), (p) => p.id.desc()])
  .limit(20)
  .all();
```

**Cursor pagination.** Call `.cursor({ field: lastValue })` after `.orderBy(...)` to resume from a known position. The cursor requires a prior `orderBy` — the type system enforces this. Direction (forward or backward) follows the sort: ascending order means "greater than the cursor value", descending means "less than".

```typescript
const page1 = await db.orm.public.Post
  .orderBy((p) => p.createdAt.desc())
  .limit(20)
  .all();

const last = page1[page1.length - 1]!;
const page2 = await db.orm.public.Post
  .orderBy((p) => p.createdAt.desc())
  .cursor({ createdAt: last.createdAt })
  .limit(20)
  .all();
```

**Ordering by a relation.** A to-one relation (`1:1`, `N:1`) exposes the related model's orderable fields; a to-many relation (`1:N`, `N:M`) exposes `count(predicate?)`, through the junction for `N:M`. One hop only. Each lowers to a correlated scalar subquery, so the main query gains no join.

```typescript
await db.orm.public.Post
  .orderBy([(p) => p.author.name.asc(), (p) => p.id.asc()])
  .all();

await db.orm.public.User
  .orderBy((u) => u.posts.count((p) => p.views.gt(10)).desc())
  .all();

await db.orm.public.User
  .orderBy((u) => u.tags.count().desc())
  .all();

await db.orm.public.User
  .orderBy((u) => u.invitedBy.name.desc({ nulls: 'last' }))
  .all();
```

A missing related row (null foreign key) orders as `NULL`. To-one relations have no `count`; to-many relations expose no fields.

Cursor keys must match fields in the active `orderBy`. For a composite `orderBy`, pass a value for each ordering column — a partial cursor seeks only on the columns you supply, which gives an incomplete keyset. An empty cursor object is a no-op: you get the unfiltered first page back. `cursor()` keys on plain columns only: it throws `ORM.ARGUMENT_INVALID` when an active order is a relation field, a relation `count(...)`, an extension-operation result (`fullTextRank`, vector distance) or sets `nulls`. `distinctOn()` throws the same only when one of its leading orders, as many as there are `distinctOn` columns, is not a plain column; relation, count and operation orders after them are fine. Paginate those orders with `.limit(n).offset(n)`.

**`.first()` vs `.first({ pk })` vs `.all()`.** Use `.first()` for a single row (issues a `LIMIT 1`); use `.first({ pk })` for primary-key lookups; reserve `.all()` for the genuine many case (no implicit `LIMIT`).

## Workflow — Eager-loading relations (`.include`)

The concept: `.include('<relation>', (branch) => branch.<chain>)` adds a relation branch to the parent query. The branch is its own collection — compose `.where` / `.select` / `.orderBy` / `.limit` on it just like the parent.

```typescript
await db.orm.public.User
  .select('id', 'email')
  .include('posts', (post) =>
    post
      .select('id', 'title', 'createdAt')
      .orderBy((p) => p.createdAt.desc())
      .limit(5),
  )
  .limit(10)
  .all();
// → Array<{ id, email, posts: Array<{ id, title, createdAt }> }>
```

**Reduce a to-many relation to a scalar.** A refinement callback may return a *reducer* — `count()`, `sum(field)`, `avg(field)`, `min(field)`, `max(field)`, plus the lossless `countBigInt()`, `sumBigInt(field)`, and `avgDecimal(field)` — instead of a collection. The parent's relation field then carries that one value rather than an array. Reducers exist only inside an `include(...)` callback; calling one elsewhere throws.

```typescript
await db.orm.public.User.include('posts', (posts) => posts.count()).all();
// → Array<{ ...user, posts: number }> — a parent with no posts reads 0

await db.orm.public.User.include('posts', (posts) => posts.sum('views')).all();
// → Array<{ ...user, posts: number | null }>

await db.orm.public.User.include('posts', (posts) => posts.avg('views')).all();
// → Array<{ ...user, posts: number | null }>

await db.orm.public.User.include('posts', (posts) => posts.min('views')).all();

```

```
86: /**
87:  * Rango del mes en horario de Bogotá (UTC−5): inicio del mes y del
88:  * siguiente, como `Temporal.Instant` (codec obligatorio del driver).
89:  * Los registros se comparan con `>= start` y `< end`.
90:  */
91: function monthRangeBogota(year: number, month: number): {
92:   start: Temporal.Instant;
93:   end: Temporal.Instant;
94: } {
95:   // 05:00 UTC del día 1 = 00:00 en Bogotá (UTC−5). JS normaliza el
96:   // overflow: mes 12 → enero del año siguiente.
97:   const start = Temporal.Instant.fromEpochMilliseconds(
98:     Date.UTC(year, month - 1, 1, 5, 0, 0),
99:   );
100:   const end = Temporal.Instant.fromEpochMilliseconds(
101:     Date.UTC(year, month, 1, 5, 0, 0),
102:   );
103:   return { start, end };
104: }
105: 
106: /** Valida y normaliza un mes/año; por defecto usa el mes actual (Bogotá). */
107: function resolveMonthYear(month?: number, year?: number) {
108:   const now = new Date();
109:   // El día actual en Bogotá: DateTimeFormat con timeZone para no depender
110:   // de la zona horaria del servidor.
111:   const bogotaParts = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
112:     timeZone: "America/Bogota",
113:     month: "numeric",
114:     year: "numeric",
115:   }).formatToParts(now);
116:   const bogotaMonth = Number(
117:     bogotaParts.find((part) => part.type === "month")?.value,
118:   );
119:   const bogotaYear = Number(
120:     bogotaParts.find((part) => part.type === "year")?.value,
121:   );
122: 
123:   const resolvedMonth = month ?? bogotaMonth;
124:   const resolvedYear = year ?? bogotaYear;
125: 
126:   if (
127:     !Number.isInteger(resolvedMonth) ||
128:     resolvedMonth < 1 ||
129:     resolvedMonth > 12
130:   ) {
131:     throw new Error("Mes inválido para las métricas financieras.");
132:   }
133:   if (!Number.isInteger(resolvedYear) || resolvedYear < 2000 || resolvedYear > 2100) {
134:     throw new Error("Año inválido para las métricas financieras.");
135:   }
136: 
137:   return { month: resolvedMonth, year: resolvedYear };
138: }
```

list implementation:

```ts
list: async ({ q, status, type, page = 1, limit = 10 }: MembershipListInput): Promise<{ rows: MembershipRow[]; total: number }> => {
  const text = (q ?? "").trim();
  const pattern = `%${escapeLike(text)}%`;
  const safePage = Math.max(1, Math.trunc(page));
  const safeLimit = Math.min(100, Math.max(1, Math.trunc(limit)));

  const now = Temporal.Instant.fromEpochMilliseconds(Date.now());
  const windowEnd = plusDays(now, EXPIRING_WINDOW_DAYS);

  let filtered = db.orm.public.Membership.where({ tenantId });
  if (type) filtered = filtered.where((m) => m.type.eq(type));
  if (status === "active") {
    filtered = filtered.where((m) => m.endDate.gt(windowEnd));
  } else if (status === "expiring") {
    filtered = filtered.where((m) => and(m.endDate.gt(now), m.endDate.lte(windowEnd)));
  } else if (status === "expired") {
    filtered = filtered.where((m) => m.endDate.lte(now));
  }
  if (text) {
    filtered = filtered.where((m) =>
      m.customer.some((c) =>
        or(c.name.ilike(pattern), c.phone.ilike(pattern), c.email.ilike(pattern)),
      ),
    );
  }

  const [rows, { total }] = await Promise.all([
    filtered
      .orderBy([(m) => m.endDate.asc(), (m) => m.id.asc()])
      .include("customer", (c) => c.select("name", "phone", "email"))
      .limit(safeLimit)
      .offset((safePage - 1) * safeLimit)
      .all(),
    filtered.aggregate((a) => ({ total: a.count() })),
  ]);

  return {
    rows: rows.map((row) => ({
      id: row.id,
      customerId: row.customerId,
      customerName: row.customer?.name ?? "Cliente eliminado",
      ...
 type: row.type,
      status: computeMembershipStatus(row.endDate),
      price: toNumber(row.price),
      startDate: String(row.startDate),
      endDate: String(row.endDate),
      createdAt: String(row.createdAt),
    })),
    total,
  };
},
```

```ts
getMetrics: async (options?: { month?: number; year?: number }): Promise<MembershipMetrics> => {
  const now = Temporal.Instant.fromEpochMilliseconds(Date.now());
  const windowEnd = plusDays(now, EXPIRING_WINDOW_DAYS);

  const [activeAgg, expiringAgg, expiredAgg] = await Promise.all([
    db.orm.public.Membership.where({ tenantId }).where((m) => m.endDate.gt(windowEnd)).aggregate((a) => ({ total: a.count() })),
    db.orm.public.Membership.where({ tenantId }).where((m) => and(m.endDate.gt(now), m.endDate.lte(windowEnd))).aggregate((a) => ({ total: a.count() })),
    db.orm.public.Membership.where({ tenantId }).where((m) => m.endDate.lte(now)).aggregate((a) => ({ total: a.count() })),
  ]);

  const { month, year } = resolveMonthYear(options?.month, options?.year);
  const { start, end } = monthRangeBogota(year, month);
  const projectionAgg = await db.orm.public.Membership
    .where({ tenantId })
    .where((m) => and(m.endDate.gte(start), m.endDate.lt(end)))
    .aggregate((a) => ({ total: a.sum("price") }));

  return {
    activeCount: activeAgg.total,
    expiringCount: expiringAgg.total,
    expiredCount: expiredAgg.total,
    renewalRevenueProjection: toNumber(projectionAgg.total),
  };
},
```

```
43: export function validatePayment(formData: FormData): PaymentValidation {

50:       (option) => option.value === rawProvider,

53:       : "",
54:     status: PAYMENT_STATUSES.some((option) => option.value === rawStatus)
55:       ? (rawStatus as PaymentStatusValue)
56:       : "",
57:     amount: String(formData.get("amount") ?? "").trim(),
58:     providerRefId: String(formData.get("providerRefId") ?? "").trim(),
59:     description: String(formData.get("description") ?? "").trim(),
60:   };
61: 
62:   const errors: PaymentFieldErrors = {};
63: 
64:   if (!PAYMENT_METHODS.some((option) => option.value === values.provider)) {
```

```
// Loader de Node para ejecutar scripts del repo con type stripping:
// - mapea el alias "@/..." → /home/craxker/github/nexus-thrive/...
// - agrega extensiones (.ts/.d.ts/.tsx/index.ts) a imports relativos sin extensión
// Uso: node --experimental-loader /tmp/opencode/nexus-loader.mjs ./script.ts
import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, resolve as resolvePath } from "node:path";
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";

const ROOT = "/home/craxker/github/nexus-thrive";

function existsAsUrl(basePath) {
  return existsSync(basePath) ? pathToFileURL(basePath).href : null;
}

export async function resolve(specifier, context, next) {
  if (specifier.startsWith("@/")) {
    const rel = specifier.slice(2);
    const plain = resolvePath(ROOT, rel);
    const candidates = [
      existsAsUrl(plain),
      existsAsUrl(plain.endsWith(".ts") ? plain : plain + ".ts"),
    ].filter(Boolean);
    if (candidates.length > 0) {
      return { url: candidates[0], shortCircuit: true };
    }
  }

  if (specifier.startsWith(".")) {
    const parent = context.parentURL ? new URL(context.parentURL).pathname : "";
    const base = resolvePath(dirname(parent), specifier);
    if (!/\.[a-z]+$/i.test(specifier)) {
      for (const ext of [".ts", ".d.ts", ".tsx"]) {
        const candidate = existsAsUrl(base + ext);
        if (candidate) {
          return { url: candidate, shortCircuit: true };
        }
      }
      const index = existsAsUrl(resolve(base, "index.ts"));
      if (index) {
        return { url: index, shortCircuit: true };
      }
    }
  }

  return next(specifier, context);
}
```

createTenant en transacción:
```ts
async createTenant(data) {
  return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
    const tenant = await tx.orm.public.Tenant.create({ name, slug, vertical, active: true });
    for (const moduleName of modules) {
      await tx.orm.public.TenantModule.create({ tenantId: tenant.id, moduleName, active: true });
    }
    return tenant;
  });
}
```

**checkSlugAvailabilityAction**: firma `(slug: string) => Promise<SlugCheck>`:
```ts
export type SlugCheck = { status: "available" | "taken" | "invalid" | "unauthorized" };
export async function checkSlugAvailabilityAction(slug: string): Promise<SlugCheck> {
  if (!(await requireSuperAdmin())) return { status: "unauthorized" };
  const validation = validateSlug(slug);
  if (!validation.ok) return { status: "invalid" };
  const exists = await createAdminDb().slugExists(validation.slug);
  return { status: exists ? "taken" : "available" };
}
```

count: number }[];\n};\n\nexport type TenantListInput = {\n  /** Host de la request actual: base para las URLs de acceso directo. */\n  host: string;\n  /** Texto libre contra name, slug o customDomain. */\n  q?: string;\n  vertical?: VerticalValue;\n  activeStatus?: \"active\" | \"inactive\" | \"all\";\n  page?: number;\n  limit?: number;\n};\n\n/** Fila serializable de tenant (fechas → string, módulos activos). */\nexport type TenantListRow = {\n  id: string;\n  name: string;\n  slug: string;\n  customDomain: string | null;\n  vertical: VerticalValue;\n  active: boolean;\n  createdAt: string;\n  /** Módulos con `active: true`, en orden del catálogo. */\n  modules: ModuleValue[];\n  /** URL de acceso directo al negocio (calculada con el host actual). */\n  url: string;\n};\n\n/** Detalle de módulos de un tenant (los 5 del catálogo con su estado). */\nexport type TenantModulesDetail = {\n  tenantId: string;\n  name: string;\n  slug: string;\n  active: boolean;\n  modules: { moduleName: ModuleValue; active: boolean }[];\n};\n\n/** Escapa los comodines de LIKE para que la búsqueda sea literal. */\nfunction escapeLike(input: string): string {\n  return input.replace(/[\\\\%_]/g, (char) => `\\\\${char}`);\n}\n\n/**\n * URL de acceso directo a un negocio.\n * - En dev (host `*.lvh.me` / `*.localhost`): subdominio\n *   `slug.<mismo host>` — sin hardcodear dominios de producción.\n * - En cualquier otro host: ruta interna multi-tenant `/{slug}`\n *   (siempre operativa vía proxy).\n */\nexport function tenantAccessUrl(slug: string, host: string): string {\n  const [hostname = \"\", port] = host.split(\":\");\n  const portSuffix = port ? `:${port}` : \"\";\n  if (hostname.endsWith(\".lvh.me\")) {\n    return `http://${slug}.lvh.me${portSuffix}/`;\n  }\n  if (hostname.endsWith(\".localhost\")) {\n    return `http://${slug}.localhost${portSuffix}/`;\n  }\n  return `/${slug}`;\n}\n\nexport function createAdminDb() {\n  return {\n    /**\n     * Autorización global: el usuario es SuperAdmin si existe una fila\n     * `User` con su `clerkUserId` y `role = SUPERADMIN`. El rol se asigna\n     * por operación de plataforma (no existe UI de auto-asignación).\n     */\n    isSuperAdmin: async (clerkUserId: string): Promise<boolean> => {\n      if (!clerkUserId) {\n        return false;\n      }\n      const user = await db.orm.public.User\n        .where({ clerkUserId, role: \"SUPERADMIN\" })\n        .first();\n      return user !== null;\n    },\n\n    /** Métricas globales de la plataforma (todas las queries en DB). */\n    getPlatformMetrics: async (): Promise<PlatformMetrics> => {\n      const count = async (filter?: {\n        active?: boolean;\n        vertical?: VerticalValue;\n      }) => {\n        let query = db.orm.public.Tenant.where({});\n        if (filter?.active !== undefined) {\n          query = query.where({ active: filter.active });\n        }\n        if (filter?.vertical) {\n          query = query.where({ vertical: filter.vertical });\n        }\n        const { total } = await query.aggregate((aggregate) => ({\n          total: aggregate.count(),\n        }));\n        return total;\n      };\n\n      const [totalTenants, activeTenants, inactiveTenants, totalUsers, byVertical] =\n        await Promise.all([\n          count(),\n          count({ active: true }),\n          count({ active: false }),\n          db.orm.public.User.aggregate((aggregate) => ({\n            total: aggregate.count(),\n          })).then((result) => result.total),\n          Promise.all(\n            VERTICALS.map(async (vertical) => ({\n              vertical,\n              count: await count({ vertical }),\n            })),\n          ),\n        ]);\n\n      return {\n        totalTenants,\n        activeTenants,\n        inactiveTenants,\n        totalUsers,\n        tenantsByVertical: byVertical,\n      };\n    },\n\n    /**\n     * Listado paginado de tenants con búsqueda (name/slug/customDomain),\n     * filtro por vertical y estado. Todo se resuelve en servidor.\n     */\n    listTenants: async ({\n      host,\n      q,\n      vertical,\n      activeStatus = \"all\",\n      page = 1,\n      limit = 10,\n    }: TenantListInput): Promise<{ rows: TenantListRow[]; total: number }> => {\n      const text = (q ?? \"\").trim();\n      const pattern = `%${escapeLike(text)}%`;\n      const safePage = Math.max(1, Math.trunc(page));\n      const safeLimit = Math.min(100, Math.max(1, Math.trunc(limit)));\n\n      let filtered = db.orm.public.Tenant.where({});\n      if (activeStatus === \"active\") {\n        filtered = filtered.where({ active: true });\n      } else if (activeStatus === \"inactive\") {\n        filtered = filtered.where({ active: false });\n      }\n      if (vertical) {\n        filtered = filtered.where({ vertical });\n      }\n      if (text) {\n        filtered = filtered.where((tenant) =>\n          or(\n            tenant.name.ilike(pattern),\n            tenant.slug.ilike(pattern),\n            tenant.customDomain.ilike(pattern),\n          ),\n        );\n      }\n\n      const [rows, { total }] = await Promise.all([\n        filtered\n          .orderBy((tenant) => tenant.createdAt.desc())\n          .include(\"modules\", (module) => module.select(\"moduleName\", \"active\"))\n          .limit(safeLimit)\n          .offset((safePage - 1) * safeLimit)\n          .all(),\n        filtered.aggregate((aggregate) => ({ total: aggregate.count() })),\n      ]);\n\n      return {\n        rows: rows.map((row) => ({\n          id: row.id,\n          name: row.name,\n          slug: row.slug,\n          customDomain: row.customDomain ?? null,\n          vertical: row.vertical,\n          active: row.active,\n          createdAt: String(row.createdAt),\n          modules: sortModules(\n            row.modules\n              .filter((module) => module.active)\n              .map((module) => module.moduleName),\n          ),\n          url: tenantAccessUrl(row.slug, host),\n        })),\n        total,\n      };\n    },\n\n    /** Disponibilidad de un slug (para el check en vivo del form). */\n    slugExists: async (slug: string): Promise<boolean> => {\n      const tenant = await db.orm.public.Tenant.where({ slug }).first();\n      return tenant !== null;\n    },\n\n    /**\n     * Alta de tenant + módulos iniciales en UNA transacción: si falla la\n     * creación de los módulos (o el insert por slug duplicado), se\n     * revierte todo — nunca quedan tenants parcialmente configurados.\n     */\n    createTenant: (data: {\n      name: string;\n      slug: string;\n      vertical: VerticalValue;\n      modules: ModuleValue[];\n    }) =>\n      db.transaction(async (tx) => {\n        const tenant = await tx.orm.public.Tenant.create({\n          name: data.name,\n          slug: data.slug,\n          vertical: data.vertical,\n        });\n\n        for (const moduleName of data.modules) {\n          await tx.orm.public.TenantModule.create({\n            tenantId: tenant.id,\n            moduleName,\n          });\n        }\n\n        return tenant;\n      }),\n\n    /** Activa o suspende un tenant. Devuelve `null` si no existe. */\n    setTenantActive: (id: string, active: boolean) =>\n      db.orm.public.Tenant.where({ id }).update({ active }),\n\n    /**\n     * Detalle de módulos de un tenant: los 5 del catálogo con su estado\n     * (los no registrados cuentan como inactivos).\n     */\n    getTenantModules: async (\n      tenantId: string,\n    ): Promise<TenantModulesDetail | null> => {\n      const tenant = await db.orm.public.Tenant\n        .where({ id: tenantId })\n        .include(\"modules\", (module) => module.select(\"moduleName\", \"active\"))\n        .first();\n\n      if (!tenant) {\n        return null;\n      }\n\n      const activeByName = new Map(\n        tenant.modules.map((module) => [module.moduleName, module.active]),\n      );\n\n      return {\n        tenantId: tenant.id,\n        name: tenant.name,\n        slug: tenant.slug,\n        active: tenant.active,\n        modules: MODULES.map((moduleName) => ({\n          moduleName,\n          active: activeByName.get(moduleName) ?? false,\n        })),\n      };\n    },\n\n    /**\n     * Crea o actualiza el estado de un módulo del tenant (upsert sobre la\n     * clave única `[tenantId, moduleName]`).\n     */\n    toggleModule: (\n      tenantId: string,\n      moduleName: ModuleValue,\n      active: boolean,\n    ) =>\n      db.orm.public.TenantModule.upsert({\n        create: { tenantId, moduleName, active },\n        update: { active },\n        conflictOn: { tenantId, moduleName },\n      }),\n  };\n}\n",

```
59: function readPrice(raw: string): { number: number; error?: string } {
60:   if (!raw) {
61:     return { number: Number.NaN, error: "Ingresa el precio." };
62:   }
63:   const amountNumber = Number(raw.replace(",", "."));
64:   if (!Number.isFinite(amountNumber) || amountNumber <= 0) {
65:     return { number: amountNumber, error: "El precio debe ser mayor que cero." };
66:   }
67:   if (amountNumber > 100_000_000) {
68:     return { number: amountNumber, error: "El precio no puede superar $100.000.000." };
69:   }
70:   return { number: amountNumber };
71: }
```

```tsx
function StatusToggle({ tenant, onNotice }) {
  const [state, formAction, isPending] = useActionState(toggleTenantStatusAction, IDLE);
  useEffect(() => { if (state.status === "ok") onNotice({kind:"success", text: state.message ?? "..."}); if (state.status==="error") onNotice({kind:"error", text: state.message ?? "..."}); }, [state, onNotice]);
  return <form action={formAction} className="inline">
    <input type="hidden" name="tenantId" value={tenant.id} />
    <input type="hidden" name="active" value={tenant.active ? "false" : "true"} />
    <button type="submit" disabled={isPending} ...>{tenant.active ? "Suspender" : "Activar"}</button>
  </form>;
}
```
Cuidado: useEffect con onNotice en deps — onNotice es setNotice (estable) ✓ si lo paso como setNotice directo. En parent: `onNotice={setNotice}` ✓ estable.

   - Si `!trimmed` → no hacer nada (pero el status quedó "checking"...). Alternativa: derivar el estado sin effect.

   Patrón mejor: usar estado `checkedSlug` en vez de `slugStatus` derivado:
   - Guardar `slugStatus` solo como resultado de la promise, y derivar visualmente: si `slug.trim() !== checkedSlug` → "checking".
   
   Diseño sin setState síncrono:
   ```ts
   const [slugCheck, setSlugCheck] = useState<{ slug: string; status: Available|Taken|Invalid } | null>(null);
   
   useEffect(() => {
     const trimmed = slug.trim();
     if (!trimmed) return;   // sin setState
     let cancelled = false;
     const timer = setTimeout(() => {
       void checkSlugAvailabilityAction(trimmed).then(result => {
         if (!cancelled && result.status !== "unauthorized") {
           setSlugCheck({ slug: trimmed, status: result.status });
         }
       });
     }, 350);
     return () => { cancelled = true; clearTimeout(timer); };
   }, [slug]);
   
   // derivado:
   const trimmed = slug.trim();
   const slugStatus: SlugStatus = !trimmed ? "idle"
     : slugCheck && slugCheck.slug === trimmed ? slugCheck.status
     : "checking";
   ```
   La promise-resolved setState está en un callback ✓ (permitido por la regla — solo prohíbe setState síncrono en el body).
 setState en `.then` es async ✓ ok.
   
   Esto elimina el error y además es más correcto (muestra "Verificando..." mientras no hay respuesta para el slug actual).

2. `cn` sin usar en tenant-module-badges → quitar import.

</details>

## Veredicto: sí puede ser MVP — y **no se filtran datos** en los vectores revisados

Lo verifiqué con evidencia, no de memoria:

### Aislamiento de datos ✅
- **Todas las rutas de tenant** pasan por `app/[tenant]/layout.tsx`: sin sesión → sign-in; tenant inexistente/inactivo → 404; **no miembro → "Sin acceso" sin renderizar datos**; el bootstrap a OWNER solo ocurre si el tenant está **vacío** (primer dueño).
- **13/13 server actions** con guard: `requireTenantDb` (sesión + tenant activo + membresía) en crm/finance/memberships, `requireSuperAdmin` en las 5 del panel admin.
- **Capa de datos única**: `createTenantDb(tenantId)` lanza si no hay tenantId, y todos los creates/queries llevan `tenantId` (FK + índice en `User`, `Customer`, `Payment`, `Expense`, `Membership`). Cada acción opera solo en su tenant aunque le mandes un slug ajeno.
- **Cero superficie API abierta**: no existen rutas `/api/*` ni webhooks.
- **Nada sensible al cliente**: ningún componente client importa `@/prisma/db`, sin `process.env` ni secretos en el bundle, sin `fetch` salientes.
- El subdominio del proxy no es confianza ciega: la app interna re-verifica membresía.

### Límites reales del MVP (no son fugas, pero conviene saberlos)
1. **Roles STAFF/OWNER sin diferenciar**: cualquier miembro puede todo dentro de su tenant. Si vas a invitar empleados, falta un `requireRole`. Con owners únicos: correcto.
2. **Carrera del primer OWNER**: el primero en visitar un tenant recién creado y vacío se lo queda. No publiques el slug antes de que entre la cuenta del dueño.
3. **Aislamiento "por disciplina"**: no hay RLS de Postgres ni filtro automático de Prisma — hoy está todo verificado, pero antes de producción seria conviene añadir RLS o tests de aislamiento tenant↔tenant.
4. `settings` e `inventory` siguen siendo **placeholders** (páginas vacías) — si el MVP los necesita, quedan pendientes.
5. Sin rate limiting propio (Clerk cubre el login).

### Estado de la base
- Eliminé el residuo `smoke-finance-*` que había quedado de un smoke antiguo: ahora la DB tiene **solo `gymcarlos`** (vertical `gym`), tus0 módulos de prueba, y tu usuario como `SUPERADMIN`.
- tsc/eslint/build ✅, smoke 55/55 ✅, gates HTTP ✅.

En corto: **para un MVP con owners únicos, la base está sana y sin fugas entre negocios**. Los puntos 1–3 son los que endurecería antes de abrirle a empleados o pasar a producción.
